# Сверка с документацией Claude Code — что доделать

Прочитано **174 из 174** страниц корпуса Claude Code целиком, через `curl -sL <url>.md`; непрочитанных нет. Корпус проверен как полный двумя путями — `llms.txt` и `sitemap.xml` дают одно и то же множество. Документация платформы вне области по решению владельца.

Заведено **245** находок уровня bug/gap. Каждая отдана независимому оппоненту с задачей её **опровергнуть**, а не подтвердить: проверить цитату дословно, открыть указанный файл, посмотреть на слой выше и слой ниже.

| Состояние | Число | Что это значит |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Выжило | **124** | Оппонент пытался опровергнуть и не смог |
| Опровергнуто | 121 | Находка неверна — сфабрикованная цитата, не та подсистема, ложное следствие, или записанное решение владельца |
| **Не оспорено** | 0 | Отдельное состояние. НЕ складывать с выжившими |

Из выживших: **28** сделано не так, **58** не сделано, **38** сделано частично.

Полный перечень расхождений, включая опровергнутые, — в `2026-08-02-claude-doc-sweep-divergences.md`.

**Номера строк в этом файле — датированное измерение, а не живой указатель.** Каждая ссылка вида `<файл>:<строка>` бралась по дереву на 2026-07-31, и с тех пор наши файлы двигались на каждом коммите. Замер 2026-08-25 по всем разрешимым ссылкам на исходники из `docs/`: 674 попадают на пустую строку, 249 — за конец файла, 959 — на одинокую `}` или `*/`. Перевешивать их на свежее дерево нельзя: перенумерованный датированный вердикт — это уже не то, что было измерено. Идентификатор — процитированное предложение и названный символ; нужен номер — перемерьте сами и поставьте свою дату. То же относится к машинным копиям `data/2026-08-02-doc-sweep-worklist.tsv` и `data/2026-08-02-doc-sweep-divergences.tsv`, у которых нет преамбулы.

**Порядок диктуется двумя словарями, а не размером.** Две единицы переписывают правила, по которым обязаны быть написаны все остальные, поэтому они идут первыми.

`managed-settings-key-vocabulary` ведёт всю настроечную половину. Она решает один раз то, что иначе будет решено по-разному в десяти планах: что делать с документированным ключом, который `refuseUnknownKeys` (managed-policy.ts:727-733) выбрасывает как неизвестный, а `StoredConfigTopLevelSchema` (validators.ts:208) отвергает так, что весь файл падает закрытым. Alias или новый ключ, strict или мягкий разбор — от этого решения зависят `managed-policy-sources`, `sandbox-path-settings`, `model-selection-defaults`, `statusline-surfaces`, `skill-visibility-settings` и `marketplace-auto-update`, каждая из которых добавляет ключи через тот же шлюз.

`hook-event-roster` ведёт всю hooks-половину. Она расширяет `AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` — версионированный инвентарь, который одновременно является словарём принимаемых значений для `automations.json` и зеркалится в предсобранный Pi-бандл. Отсюда следует правило релизного порядка (конфиг с новым именем события падает на старой сборке; host и subprocess едут из одной сборки), и это правило обязаны соблюдать три остальных hooks-плана. Дальше hooks идут строго цепочкой, потому что все они правят `automations/types.ts` и `lifecycle-bridge.ts`, а `git commit <pathspec>` берёт состояние рабочего дерева: `hook-input-payload-parity` → `hook-output-and-process-env`, и отдельно `hook-firing-and-await` — позже всех, о нём ниже.

**Затем настроечная волна**, от общего к частному: `managed-policy-sources` (каналы и правило «источники не сливаются»), `sandbox-path-settings`, `model-selection-defaults`, `statusline-surfaces`. Все четыре — persistence и delivered-policy, то есть risk trigger; ни одна не может быть написана до того, как словарь ключей зафиксирован.

**Память** идёт своей цепочкой, и её первый шаг обязателен: `memory-load-limits` переносит лимит в 200 строк на маршрут, которым читается каждый ход, и вводит отсутствующие 25KB. Пока этого нет, `memory-import-recognition` и `memory-write-feedback` меняли бы то, что не измеряется. Замыкает `memory-discovery-scopes` — она правит тот же `native-sources.ts`.

**MCP** — `mcp-server-config-and-connect` первым, потому что он определяет, что вообще может сказать конфиг сервера и с каким env/headers мы подключаемся; на нём стоят `mcp-roots-and-channels` (тот же `client.ts`) и `tool-result-size-thresholds`.

**Headless CLI** идёт после MCP по содержательной причине: `headless-init-frame` обязан заполнить `mcp_server_errors`, а какие конфиги считаются ошибочными, решает предыдущая единица. За ним `headless-cli-flags-and-exit` — тот же `apps/cli/src/index.ts`, и байтовый cap должен считать уже существующий init-кадр.

**Здесь становится понятен единственный неочевидный порядок:** `hook-firing-and-await` идёт после headless, а не рядом с остальными hooks. Ему нужен launch mode (`--init-only`, `-p --init`, `-p --maintenance`), которого в продукте нет, то есть новый флаг в том же файле CLI и новое поле в session-create RPC. Дешевле добавить флаг к уже зафиксированному контракту флагов, чем наоборот. Это же самая опасная единица набора: она меняет смысл уже сохранённых записей `automations.json` без изменения схемы — сохранённый catch-all `Setup` перестаёт срабатывать каждую сессию.

**Оркестрация** имеет свой локальный ведущий: `subagent-nesting-depth` (глубина 1 против документированных 3) обязан лечь первым, потому что фикстуры и арифметика семафоров всех следующих планов написаны под текущую глубину. Далее `subagent-limits-and-child-output`, `agent-memory-directories` (ждёт ещё и memory-планов — общий `memory-store.ts`), `agent-definition-fields`, `workflow-invocation-contract`.

**Skills и команды** — `skill-visibility-settings` первой: в ней оседает семантика `disable-model-invocation`/`user-invocable`, которую потом потребляют `skill-frontmatter-runtime`, `skill-discovery-precedence`, `custom-command-expansion` и `code-review-contract`. Рядом, независимо, `builtin-session-commands` (`/clear`, `/btw`, `/recap` — один парсер и один wire-union) и `shell-command-response-mode`.

**Worktrees и расписания** — `worktree-lifecycle` перед `scheduled-task-catchup` (запуску по расписанию нужен worktree); `loop-and-self-paced-scheduling` независима, это другой планировщик (`shared/sessions/cron-*`, а не `shared/automations/*`).

**Плагины** — `marketplace-auto-update` → `plugin-install-and-dependencies` → `plugin-bundle-component-shapes` (последняя ждёт ещё и `statusline-surfaces`: плагинный `subagentStatusLine` некуда направить, пока механизма нет).

**Независимые, и одну из них стоит взять раньше формального места в списке.** `egress-and-provider-routing` содержит утечку: 30x от гейтвея сегодня пересылает JWT на третий хост, потому что на двух fetch-вызовах нет `redirect: 'error'`. Формально она ни от чего не зависит и может ехать в любой волне — но это единственная строка набора, где цена ожидания измеряется в утёкшем секрете. Тем же свойством обладают `deep-link-safety` (ссылка извне процесса дёргает state-mutating RPC без действия пользователя) и `project-trust-home-carveout` ($HOME получает постоянный grant).

Остальные независимые — `permission-tool-classification`, `output-styles`, `claude-informational-messages`, `keybindings-config`, `goal-completion-state`, `web-search-budget`, `host-diagnostics-rpc` — можно ставить куда угодно, при одном ограничении: многие из них трогают `apps/cli/src/index.ts` или `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts`, и по правилу зонирования по файлам две такие единицы не идут параллельно.

## Развёрнуто по каждой позиции

### сделано не так · hooks

#### f002 · `hooks`

Two documented keys are wrong or missing on the FileChanged stdin payload. (1) Key name only: the absolute-path field is spelled `path`, the doc spells it `file_path` — the value is the same idea, so this is a rename, except that our value is not guaranteed absolute (no `resolve()` against the session cwd) and is absent when uncorrelated. (2) Missing field: `event` (`change`|`add`|`unlink`) is never emitted at all, and the extra `change_kind` (the mutating tool name) is a Nessy invention with no documented counterpart. Because `hookCommandStdinPayload` spreads the input verbatim, a hook doing `jq -r .file_path` reads `null` and `jq -r .event` reads `null`. Separately, and narrower than the doc rather than contradicting a field: the trigger is tool completion over four write tools, not a filesystem watch, so `unlink` is structurally unreachable (a deletion, or any edit made by bash/an external editor, never fires the event), the matcher never builds a watch list, and the documented `watchPaths` output field is unimplemented anywhere in src (`grep -ran watchPaths packages/*/src apps/electron/src` returns nothing).

- **Документация связывает.** hooks.md § FileChanged input: "In addition to the common input fields, FileChanged hooks receive `file_path` and `event`" — `file_path` is the "Absolute path to the file that changed" and `event` is "`\"change\"` for a modified file, `\"add\"` for a created file, or `\"unlink\"` for a deleted file". The JSON example on the page shows exactly those two keys alongside the common fields. The event itself "Runs when a watched file changes on disk", has no decision control, and its matcher both builds the literal watch list and filters on the changed file's basename.
  > In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), FileChanged hooks receive `file_path` and `event`.
- **У нас.** The only emitter of FileChanged is the Pi lifecycle bridge. It fires on successful completion of a file-mutating TOOL, not on a disk watch: `FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS = new Set(['write','edit','replace_in_file','multi_edit'])` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:52); the tool's path argument is stashed on `tool_execution_start` (lifecycle-bridge.ts:194-197, via `mutatedPath` at :85-89, which reads `record.path ?? record.file_path ?? record.filePath`) and replayed on `tool_execution_end` (lifecycle-bridge.ts:224-233) as `await options.emit('FileChanged', { hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: toolName, ...(path ? { path } : {}) })`. So the payload carries `change_kind` (the tool name, e.g. `write`) and `path`, never `file_path` and never `event`. The path is passed through verbatim with no `resolve()` — there is no `node:path` import in the file (only a `.join('\n')` on an array at lifecycle-bridge.ts:135) — so it is absolute only if the model happened to pass an absolute argument, and it is omitted entirely when the start/end correlation captured nothing. Nothing downstream re-keys it: the payload crosses the subprocess wire as `OutboundAutomationEvent` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:498, sent at :1969 and :2958), is forwarded verbatim by pi-agent.ts:2325 → `BaseAgent.emitAutomationEvent` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1438-1459) → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (packages/shared/src/automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:14-29), and reaches a command hook's stdin through `hookCommandStdinPayload`, which spreads `...input` and adds only `hook_event_name` and `cwd` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651). The type declares the fork's spelling: `path?: string; change_kind?: string;` under "Filesystem change events" (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:804-805), and the frozen contract row declares `redactedPayload: ['change_kind']` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:73). The one place that knows the documented spelling is read-side only: `changedFileBasename` reads `input.file_path ?? input.path` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:150-154), used by `getMatchValueForSdkInput`'s `case 'FileChanged'` (utils.ts:218-220), so the matcher works today purely through the `?? input.path` fallback. The shape is frozen by tests: packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:90 asserts `toEqual({ hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: 'write', path: '/repo/sub/a.txt' })`, packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:641-643 and packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/hooks-automation.test.ts:621-624 build inputs with `path`/`change_kind`.
- **Пользователь.** Observable, and it makes an imported Claude plugin look broken rather than absent. Install a Claude plugin whose `hooks.json` declares a FileChanged hook — the documented example shape is a `.envrc`/`.env` reloader, and formatter-on-save hooks are the same pattern — then have the agent write that file with the write/edit tool. The hook DOES fire and its matcher DOES match (the basename comes from the `path` fallback), so the user sees the hook run and any stderr surface; but the script's `jq -r .file_path` (or `$file_path`) yields the string `null`, so it formats nothing, reloads nothing, or errors on a path named "null". Any `event`-conditional branch (`if [ "$event" = "add" ]`) never takes, since the key is absent on every emission. A user writing their own Nessy automation from our docs hits the same wall from the other side: docs-site documents the event but no fields, so copying a Claude example is the natural move. Latent parts, for honesty: deleting a file, editing one through bash, or an external editor touching a watched file produces no event at all — that surfaces only for a user who expects a real disk watcher, and no `watchPaths`-returning hook can work at all today.
- **Правка.**
  - `packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts` `createPiLifecycleExtension / PiLifecycleBridgeOptions / mutatedPath` — Emit the documented payload. (a) Add `cwd: string` to `PiLifecycleBridgeOptions` (:28-36) — the session cwd, used as the resolution base. (b) Import `resolve` from `node:path` and `existsSync` from `node:fs` (the file currently imports neither; it runs in the Node subprocess so both are available). (c) Change `pendingFilePaths` (:101) from `Map<string, string | undefined>` to `Map<string, { filePath?: string; existed: boolean }>`; at `tool_execution_start` (:194-197) compute `const raw = mutatedPath(event?.args)`, `const abs = raw ? resolve(options.cwd, raw) : undefined`, and store `{ filePath: abs, existed: abs ? existsSync(abs) : false }`. (d) At `tool_execution_end` (:227-233) replace the emit body with `{ hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', ...(abs ? { file_path: abs, event: pending.existed ? 'change' : 'add' } : {}) }`; delete `change_kind` and `path`. Keep the existing omit-when-unknown behaviour for the path rather than inventing one — note for the implementer: such an emission is unmatchable (empty basename) and suppressing it entirely is the defensible alternative; pick one deliberately. (e) Extend the comment at :51-52 to record that `unlink` is unreachable while the trigger is tool completion over FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS, so a reader does not file it as a missing value.
  - `packages/pi-agent-server/src/compat/pi-runtime-adapter.ts` `createSession → createPiLifecycleExtension call` — One line: pass `cwd` into the options object at :270-274. `cwd` is already destructured from `options` at :259 and is the same value handed to `createExecutor`/`createResourceLoader`, so no new plumbing.
  - `packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts` `SdkAutomationInput, AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` — Re-key the declared payload. Delete `change_kind?: string` (:805) and the FileChanged use of `path?: string` (:804) — nothing else on this interface reads either (see blastRadius: the many `input.path` hits elsewhere are tool_input records, a different type). Add `event?: 'change' | 'add' | 'unlink';` with a comment quoting hooks.md § FileChanged input and stating that `unlink` is currently unreachable. Extend the existing `file_path?: string` doc block (:806-820, written for InstructionsLoaded) to say FileChanged uses the same key for the absolute changed path. Update the frozen contract row at :73 from `redactedPayload: ['change_kind']` to `redactedPayload: ['event']` (the path stays off the declared-safe list, as today).
  - `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts` `changedFileBasename` — One line: drop the `?? input.path` fallback at :151 once the emitter is fixed, so a single spelling remains. Optional and safely deferrable — leaving it costs nothing but keeps a key nothing produces.

#### f001 · `hooks`

Three deltas, and none of them is a key rename.

1. Firing rule inverted. The doc says Setup does not fire on normal startup and fires only under `--init-only` / `-p --init` / `-p --maintenance`. Nessy fires it on every Pi `session_start` (`lifecycle-bridge.ts:104-107`), i.e. on ordinary startup, which is the exact case the doc excludes.
2. The documented key is absent, not misspelled. The payload carries `source: 'pi-runtime'` and `lifecycle_version: 1` and no `trigger` at all (`lifecycle-bridge.ts:107`, frozen at `automations/types.ts:38`). `source` is not a renamed `trigger`: `pi-runtime` is not one of the two legal values, and `source` is separately the documented matcher field of `SessionStart` (`utils.ts:190-191`), so re-reading `source` as Setup's trigger would collide.
3. The gate the value would come from does not exist. There is no launch mode in the product to derive `init` vs `maintenance` from (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:77-140`), so this cannot be fixed at the emitter alone — the trigger has to be introduced at the CLI and carried to the host.

Downstream of those: Setup's matcher is inert (`utils.ts:238`, `hooks-automation.ts:347`), so an imported Claude Setup hook is all-or-nothing — catch-all hooks over-fire once per session, correctly-matched (`init`/`maintenance`) hooks never fire.

- **Документация связывает.** hooks.md#setup binds two things at once. (1) Firing: "Fires only when you launch Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag. It doesn't fire on normal startup." (hooks.md:1061), with the matcher table at hooks.md:1063-1067 mapping matcher `init` -> `claude --init-only` / `claude -p --init` and matcher `maintenance` -> `claude -p --maintenance`. (2) Payload: "In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field set to either `\"init\"` or `\"maintenance\"`" (hooks.md:1085), and the example body carries exactly `"hook_event_name": "Setup", "trigger": "init"` (hooks.md:1088-1094). The matcher field for Setup is therefore `trigger`, and its only two legal values are `init` and `maintenance`.

- **Пользователь.** Observable today, in three distinct ways.

1. Over-firing. Four distinct deltas; only one is a key-name problem.

1. TRIGGER (the real defect). Documented occurrences are settings-file / managed-policy / skill-file changes. Ours are runtime session-config commits (`model`, `authType`, `providerType`, `runtime`, `thinkingLevel`). The two sets are DISJOINT: no settings-file edit produces an occurrence at all, so even `"matcher": "*"` never sees one; and every occurrence we do produce is one the page never describes.

2. PAYLOAD. Documented `source` (required, five-value vocabulary) + optional `file_path`; ours `config_keys: string[]` + `config_digest`. This is NOT a key rename with a right value behind it — the values do not exist anywhere in the process at emit time. Both documented field names already exist on `SdkAutomationInput` (`types.ts:754`, `:820`) and are simply never set for this event, so this is a producer gap, not a schema gap.

3. MATCHER. `getMatchValueForSdkInput` returning `''` (`utils.ts:221-239`) is a CONSEQUENCE of 1+2 and is a recorded, tested, author-diagnosed decision (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:155-165`) — correct given today's payload, and wrong only once the producer lands. Do not "fix" the matcher on its own: it would then read a field nothing sets.

4. BLOCKING. Documented: a block prevents the change taking effect, except `policy_settings`. Ours: advisory receipt after the change is already committed (`pi-agent.ts:7331-7341`). For the file-driven occurrences the documented semantics ARE reachable — skip the in-memory reload — which the runtime-config path could not do.

A user who writes a ConfigChange hook — natively in `hooks.json`, or by installing a Claude plugin that ships one — gets one of two wrong outcomes:

(1) With any documented matcher (`"matcher": "project_settings"`, `user_settings`, `skills`, `policy_settings`, `local_settings`), the hook NEVER runs. Nessy does warn at install/registration time (`plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches`), so it is not silent, but the hook is dead.

(2) With a catch-all matcher, the hook DOES run — on the wrong occurrences. It fires when the user picks a different model in the composer, changes thinking level, or a connection runtime refreshes; it does NOT fire when they edit `~/.nessy-agent/config.json`, the workspace `hooks.json`/`automations.json`/`permissions.json`, a `SKILL.md`, or when managed gateway settings refresh. The `audit-config-change.sh` recipe printed in hooks.md § ConfigChange therefore writes an audit log with no `source`, no `file_path`, and no settings-file entries at all — it logs model switches instead.

For this fork specifically, the missing occurrence is the one `server-managed-settings.md:277` names as the mechanism to log or block unauthorised changes to managed policy: that tamper-detection path has nothing to fire on. And because the block is advisory (`pi-agent.ts:7331-7341`), even a hook that does fire cannot prevent anything.

Three deltas, all on one event; none is a key-name mismatch — there is no value being carried under a wrong key.

1. WRONG OCCURRENCE. Documented trigger is "a user-typed command expands into a prompt"; ours is "a turn is about to be sent" (`pi-agent.ts:6565` → `:6418`). It over-fires on every plain prompt with no command, and it is keyed to the turn, not to the expansion.
2. EMPTY PAYLOAD. All five documented fields (`expansion_type`, `command_name`, `command_args`, `command_source`, `prompt`) are absent from the emission AND from the `SdkAutomationInput` type. Command hooks read stdin as a spread of that input (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-651`), so a hook script reading `command_name` gets `undefined`.

### сделано не так · mcp

#### f038 · `agent-sdk/mcp`

Three deltas, in descending size. (a) THE NUMBER: our MCP persist threshold is 12,000 estimated tokens, the doc's is 25,000 — so every MCP result in the ~12k–25k token band (roughly 48KB–100KB of plain text) is taken off the model and replaced with a file reference where Claude Code hands it over inline. On the Claude backend and on the local-tools path the effective number is lower still, `min(12000, 10% of the model's context window)` with a 2,000-token floor, because the second guard passes `contextWindow`. (b) THE OVERRIDE IS ABSENT, not misnamed: there is no `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` and no `NESSY_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` — nothing reads any env var here, so a user who follows Claude's docs and exports `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=50000` gets no effect whatsoever. (c) COMPOSITION OF THE PER-TOOL ANNOTATION: the value and the 500,000-char ceiling are right, only the composition differs — mcp.md:1023/:1054 says a declaring tool uses its value "instead" of the token limit for text content, ours only raises (large-response.ts:625-628), so a server declaring a value BELOW the default is not honoured downward; and because the Claude/local-tools second guard never receives `maxResultSizeChars`, a declared allowance that legitimately kept a 120,000-char result inline in the pool is re-persisted one layer up, defeating the annotation on those backends.

- **Документация связывает.** agent-sdk/mcp.md:891 — "The SDK applies the same MCP output limit as Claude Code. When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions. Raise the limit with the MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable." The linked page it defers to for "the full behavior" fixes the detail: mcp.md:1022 "the default maximum is 25,000 tokens", :1021 the limit is adjusted via `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, :1023 the env var "applies to tools that don't declare their own limit. Tools that set `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` use that value instead for text content, regardless of what `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is set to", and :1040 that annotation is honoured "up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters".
  > When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions.
- **У нас.** The persist-to-disk mechanism itself matches: an MCP result is guarded in `McpClientPool.callTool` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2170-2178) via `guardLargeResult`, which saves the full text under `<session>/long_responses/` and returns a replacement message naming the absolute path (packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts:634-641, :666-671, :700-708). The NUMBER is wrong and the override is absent. (1) The MCP call site passes `maxResultSizeChars` but no `contextWindow` (mcp-pool.ts:2171-2177), so the threshold is `tokenLimitFor(undefined)` = `TOKEN_LIMIT` = 12000 estimated tokens (large-response.ts:42, :141-147, :633). (2) No env override exists anywhere: `grep -ran MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` over the repo (binary-safe, node_modules/.references/dist excluded) hits only docs JSON, and there is no `NESSY_`-prefixed counterpart; large-response.ts contains no `process.env` read at all. This is not a rename artifact — the fork does port sibling knobs under its own prefix (`NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` at mcp-pool.ts:1959; the `CLAUDE_CODE_*` → `NESSY_*` mapping table at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:9-12). (3) Two SECOND guards re-decide the same MCP result at an even lower threshold and without the per-tool annotation: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1829-1835 guards every `tool_result` event with `contextWindow` and no `maxResultSizeChars` — and MCP proxy tools reach it, because the Claude backend serves them from an SDK MCP server whose handler returns `pool.callTool`'s text (claude-agent.ts:616-624) and `createToolResult` has no MCP exclusion (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/base-event-adapter.ts:205-221); packages/shared/src/agent/local-tools/runtime.ts:59 → :338-352 does the same for `executeMcpTool` results (:289-295). `tokenLimitFor` with a context window can only LOWER the limit — `Math.min(TOKEN_LIMIT, 10% of window)`, floor 2000 (large-response.ts:141-147). (4) The per-tool annotation is read and clamped correctly (`anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` at mcp-pool.ts:213 and :1933-1940, ceiling `MAX_DECLARED_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS = 500_000` at large-response.ts:57, clamp at :620-624) but composes as raise-only: `if (declaredAllowance !== undefined && text.length <= declaredAllowance) return null` (:625-628), then the normal check still runs.
- **Пользователь.** Concrete and reachable today. Call any MCP tool that returns a mid-sized text payload — a GitHub issue list, a DB schema dump, a Confluence/Jira page fetch, a `tools/list`-style inventory — sized roughly 48KB–100KB. In Claude Code the agent receives it inline; in Nessy the chat shows the tool returning a `[Response too large]`-style replacement naming a `long_responses/…txt` path plus an LLM summary, and the agent has to spend an extra turn Reading the file back, with whatever the summary dropped simply gone from the turn. On the Claude backend, or any model with a context window under 120k, it bites earlier still — the second guard scales the limit to 10% of the window (floor 2,000 tokens), so an ~8KB MCP result already spills on a 64k-window model. And the documented escape hatch does not exist: a user who reads Claude's docs and exports `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=50000` sees exactly no change, with no warning that the variable is unrecognised. Separately, a server that declared `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` to keep its big result inline gets that honoured by the pool and then undone one layer up on the Claude and local-tools backends, so the annotation appears not to work.

#### f135 · `channels-reference`

Two wrong strings on the ingress, plus one field that has nowhere to go. (1) The registered method literal is `claude/channel` where the contract says `notifications/claude/channel` — the value we used is real, but it is the capability key, not the method, so the prefix is simply missing. (2) The param read is `params.text` where the contract says `params.content` — again only the key name is wrong; the value's meaning, sanitization and 32 KiB bound are all correct and can be kept as-is. (3) `meta` is absent at the type level, not merely unread: `McpChannelMessage` carries no field for it and the pool guard would reject nothing but also preserve nothing. Because MCP dispatch is an exact string map with no fallback handler here, (1) alone means a doc-conforming channel server has every event dropped with no error and no log; (2) means even a server that used our un-prefixed method would still be ignored unless it happened to send `text`. Nothing in the repo emits either form (`grep -arn 'claude/channel'` over source finds only client.ts:113 plus prose in docs-site), so there is no in-house producer to stay compatible with.

- **Документация связывает.** A channel server pushes events with the JSON-RPC notification method `notifications/claude/channel`, whose params are `content` (string, the event body) and optional `meta` (`Record<string, string>`, each entry becoming an attribute on the `<channel>` tag; keys must be identifiers of letters, digits and underscores only, other keys are silently dropped) — channels-reference.md:48, :221, :225, :229-230. The bare string `claude/channel` is a DIFFERENT thing on that page: it is only the capability key `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']` (:198, :212), whose presence is what registers the listener.
  > Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:

For kind `skill`, the global (user) scope must outrank the project scope when picking the unqualified alias; today `scopeSpecificity` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869) puts project above global. Nothing else is wrong: retention is right (both records kept, addressable by qualified key), the diagnostic is right, builtin stays last as skills.md:122 requires, and the subagent/MCP arms are right as they are. This is NOT a global inversion of `scopeSpecificity` — that function also produces the layer `order` for instruction and permission merging (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:967, :985), where project-last is correct, and it feeds the MCP arm where nearest-scope wins. The fix must be kind-scoped to `skill`, and must not lift `builtin` above `project`, so it is not a plain reversal of the four-value chain.

- **Документация связывает.** features-overview.md:193 binds name-collision resolution per component type: "**Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents)." So for a SKILL the user-level (personal) definition must win the bare name over a project-level one — the inverse of the subagent order, where project beats user. skills.md:122 states the same rule independently ("enterprise overrides personal, and personal overrides project") and adds that a skill at any of those levels overrides a bundled skill of the same name, i.e. bundled/builtin always loses.

Not a naming mismatch, not a missing mechanism: an enforcement path that works, set to the wrong number with nothing able to change it. The value was deliberately chosen for parity when the page documented a default of 1 (v2.1.217-218); the page moved to 3 in v2.1.219 and we did not.

- **Документация связывает.** agent-sdk/subagents.md:190 — "By default, subagents can spawn subagents of their own, up to three layers below the main conversation. Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed." sub-agents.md:862 adds the at-limit rule: "At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork ... A fork at the limit keeps `Agent` in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning." So we are bound to (a) a default ceiling of three subagent layers, and (b) an env-var override honouring `1` as "nesting off".

#### f095 · `workflows`

The value is wrong, not the key: `args` is spelled correctly and reaches the script correctly whenever it is supplied — the only delta is the substitution performed when it is NOT supplied. Claude leaves the global `undefined`; we hand the script `{}` (workflow-tool.ts:750 and :660), and on the slash path we hand it `{ input: '' }` (sessions.ts:337-340). Consequence: every documented no-input branch (`args === undefined`, `!args`, `args ?? default`) is unreachable, because `{}` is both defined and truthy. In the opposite direction our behaviour is more lenient than the spec — `args.foo` yields `undefined` here where Claude throws a TypeError — so no script errors out; it silently takes the wrong branch.

- **Документация связывает.** workflows.md:227 binds the `args` global to the invocation value verbatim: "Claude passes the list as structured data, so the script can call array and object methods on `args` directly without parsing it first. If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script." So a saved or plugin workflow run with no input must see `args === undefined`, which is what makes the `args ?? default`, `if (!args)` and `args === undefined` idioms in a script work.
  > If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script.
- **У нас.** The workflow runtime coalesces an omitted `args` to an empty object at BOTH invocation chokepoints. Top-level run: `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}));` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:750). Nested in-script helper: `return await compileWorkflowScript(source)(makeApi(recipeArgs ?? {}));` (workflow-tool.ts:660). Nothing else defaults it — `normalizeInput` carries the value through unchanged (`args: params.args`, workflow-tool.ts:186), the tool schema marks it optional ('Optional JSON value exposed inside the script as args.', workflow-tool.ts:436), `makeApi` assigns it straight onto the api (`args: runtimeArgs`, workflow-tool.ts:728), and the sandbox injects `api.args` verbatim as the `args` Function parameter (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/sandbox.ts:285, :297, :345). Measured on this HEAD by compiling `return JSON.stringify({typeofArgs: typeof args, isUndefined: args === undefined, falsy: !args, nullishDefault: (args ?? 'DEFAULT-BRANCH')})` through the real `compileWorkflowScript`: with our call-site expression (`undefined ?? {}`) → {"typeofArgs":"object","isUndefined":false,"falsy":false,"nullishDefault":{}}; positive control, the same script with the value passed through unmodified → {"typeofArgs":"undefined","isUndefined":true,"falsy":true,"nullishDefault":"DEFAULT-BRANCH"}. A second, independent chokepoint sits one layer up on the user-facing path: the slash-command RPC always attaches args, even when the user typed no tail — `const args = message.trim()` then `workflowInvocation = { ...command.workflowInvocation, args: { input: args } }` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:322, :337-340), so `/my-workflow` with no trailing text reaches the tool as `args = { input: '' }`. The command records themselves carry no args (`workflowInvocation: { name: recipe.meta.name }` for saved workflows, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:15881; `workflowInvocation: { script: parsed.source }` for plugin workflows, SessionManager.ts:16158), so the RPC layer is the sole producer. Both paths funnel into workflow-tool.ts:750, and saved (`name`) and plugin (`scriptPath`/`script`) sources resolve into the same run (workflow-tool.ts:236-243, :750).
- **Пользователь.** Today, running a saved or plugin workflow with no input never takes its no-input path. Concretely: the user types `/release-audit` in the composer with no trailing text; the RPC layer sends `args: { input: '' }` (sessions.ts:337-340) and, on the tool-call route, the runtime substitutes `{}` (workflow-tool.ts:750). A script written to Claude's documented idiom — `const target = args ?? 'HEAD'`, or `if (!args) { return usage() }`, or `const files = args === undefined ? await discover() : args.files` — silently takes the has-input branch and runs against `{}`/`''`: agents get prompts with a blank target, a fan-out over an empty list produces zero or one empty item, and the run reports success. No error surfaces anywhere, so the user sees a workflow that 'ran' and did nothing useful, with nothing in the transcript naming the cause. This is not hypothetical for imported content — Claude plugin workflows are loaded verbatim and are exactly the scripts written to that page's idiom. For workflows our own model authors it is latent, because the prompt guidance tells it to read `args.input` (workflow-tool.ts:410, :413) rather than to branch on absence.

#### f084 · `sub-agents`

Two deltas, both on the same doc sentence, plus one absent knob. (a) VALUE: the nesting budget defaults to 1 where the page says 3. Depth 1 is precisely Claude's documented 'nesting off' setting, so we ship the off configuration as the default. Nothing about the mechanism, the field name (`orchestrator.depth` → `budgets.maxDepth`) or the enforcement point is wrong — only the number. (b) MISSING OVERRIDE: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` has no reader and no Nessy-spelled equivalent, so the value cannot be changed by a user at all; the doc's `settings.json` `env` example has no effect. This half is not-built, not mis-valued. (c) WITHHOLDING RULE INVERTED IN SCOPE: the page withholds `Agent` from a subagent AT THE LIMIT; we subtract `subagent` from every tool-less subagent's inherited pool at every depth (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:141`) and, for an agent that names it explicitly, return `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` at call time — which is the page's FORK behaviour applied to named subagents. At today's limit of 1 the two layers happen to agree; raising (a) alone would change nothing observable, because (c) still keeps `Agent` out of every default subagent's pool. That coupling is the reason this is one fix and not two.

- **Документация связывает.** sub-agents.md § *Let subagents spawn their own subagents*: "By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation. At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork, so a subagent at the limit does its delegated work itself and returns one summary. A fork at the limit keeps `Agent` in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning." The limit is configurable: "To change the limit, set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to the number of subagent layers you want below your main conversation", "Set `1` to turn nesting off", and env-vars.md's row for that variable adds "(default: 3) … Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed." Per-agent opt-out is by definition, not by global default: "To keep one subagent from spawning while nesting is on … omit `Agent` from its `tools` list or add it to `disallowedTools`."
  > By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.

Not a wrong key name — a missing second limit plus a wrong failure mode. Four deltas: (1) SCOPE — one semaphore serves both the Agent-tool path and the workflow path, where the doc specifies two independent ceilings (:911); the workflow number (16, narrowed by `cpuCores - 2`) is correct for workflows and is being applied to subagents. (2) THRESHOLD — the subagent ceiling should be 20 flat; ours is `min(16, cpuCores - 2)`, i.e. 6 on an 8-core machine, 2 on a 4-core one. (3) FAILURE MODE — an over-limit Agent-tool spawn must FAIL with `Concurrent subagent limit reached` and a do-not-retry instruction; ours blocks in a FIFO queue and eventually succeeds, so the model never learns it over-fanned-out. (4) MISSING CONTROLS — no `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` equivalent (the repo's mapping convention would make it `NESSY_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, cf. `NESSY_FORK_SUBAGENT` at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:54-56), no ultracode exemption, and no `/subtask` exemption (:908) — ours can block a user-started fork behind a background fan-out. Resume is already effectively unchecked, so :909 needs no change. Secondary: the doc's limit is per SESSION; ours is per Pi subprocess, and `SessionManager.ts:11143` min-clamps a nested child's inherited `concurrency`, so a deep tree's total running count is not bounded by any single counter.

- **Документация связывает.** sub-agents.md:904 (§ Concurrent subagent limit) binds the Agent-tool spawn path to a per-session ceiling of 20 RUNNING subagents that FAILS the spawn with the message `Concurrent subagent limit reached` and tells the model not to retry; the ceiling is overridable through `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (any positive whole number) and is not enforced at all in a session with ultracode (max effort) active. :908 exempts an in-session `/subtask` fork — it 'takes a slot while it runs and is never blocked by the limit'; :909 lets a resume take a fresh slot without a check; :911 says agents other features run — workflow agents, agent-team teammates — 'follow their own limits instead', i.e. the subagent ceiling and the workflow ceiling are two limits, not one.
  > By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry.
- **У нас.** One module-level FIFO semaphore gates every child spawn in the Pi subprocess. `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:103) is narrowed at runtime to `Math.max(1, Math.min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2))` (spawner.ts:136-142), and the singleton is built from it at spawner.ts:204 and rebuilt per capability generation at spawner.ts:208. Every spawn body — start, plus the background `monitorWithAbort` wait, so a slot is held for the child's whole life — runs inside `semaphore.run` at spawner.ts:587-649. An over-limit caller is QUEUED, never refused: `Semaphore.acquire` (spawner.ts:165-186) pushes a waiter and rejects only on an aborted signal. All five spawn paths share that one gate: the Agent tool (subagent-tool.ts:282, :316), workflow `agent()` (workflow-tool.ts:358, :390 via the `spawn` resolved at :466), review (review-tool.ts:309), guardian judge (guardian-runner.ts:57) and the `/subtask` fork (subtask.ts:95). The value 16 and the CPU narrowing are exactly the WORKFLOW contract (workflows.md:320, 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores'), so the subagent half sits 4 below spec and shares a limit the doc says is separate. There is no env reader: `grep -ra` over packages/ apps/ returns zero hits for `MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` and zero source hits for `Concurrent subagent limit`; `concurrency` reaches the subprocess only as `PiOrchestratorConfig.concurrency` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:30, default 16 at :103, validated at :250), which no host code ever sets — SessionManager.ts:4152 builds the manifest seed without it. Resume is outside the gate entirely (subagent-tool.ts:474 calls `childSessionPort.resume`, and the host's `resume` flips status back to `running` with no concurrency check, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:216-234). - **Пользователь.** Observable, on the fan-out that Nessy advertises. The effective subagent cap is `min(16, cores - 2)`: 6 on a typical 8-core laptop, 2 on a 4-core one. A `subagent` parallel call with 12 tasks starts 6 and silently queues the other 6 — no error, no badge, no reason shown — so a wave Claude Code would run at once takes two or three, and the model, never seeing a refusal, keeps requesting fan-outs the machine will serialize. There is no user or admin knob to raise it. Worse and sharper: `/subtask` blocks. `startSubtaskFork` awaits admission (subtask.ts:137-142) through the same semaphore, so while a background fan-out holds every slot, the user's `/subtask` produces no fork panel and no error until a slot frees — the doc's exact promise is that this fork is 'never blocked by the limit'. Nothing in the product ever prints `Concurrent subagent limit reached`.

(1) VALUE: our default and effective ceiling is 1 where env-vars.md:280 says 3, i.e. we ship the page's documented "set `1` to turn nesting off" configuration as the unconditional product behaviour. This was correct parity for v2.1.217-2.1.218 and was chosen for that reason; v2.1.219 moved the page to 3 and our value did not move. A subagent cannot delegate at all: the ceiling is one layer below the main conversation and there is no way for a user to lift it. Two surfaces. (1) The common case is silent — an agent (the user's own or one imported from a Claude/Codex plugin) that declares no `tools` list never receives `subagent` at all (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:141`), so a reviewer agent asked to "dispatch a verifier per finding" quietly does the whole job itself in one context: the user sees a flatter, slower, more context-hungry run and no message explaining why. (2) The explicit case is a visible mid-run tool error — an author who lists `subagent`/`Agent` in the agent's `tools` gets `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` back from the first delegation, in the subagent's transcript. In both cases the documented remedy does not work: setting `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (or any Nessy spelling) in the environment or a settings `env` block has no effect, because nothing reads it — a user porting a Claude Code setup that relies on a two- or three-layer agent tree gets a silently flattened run with no diagnostic and no knob.

#### f021 · `tools-reference`

Value right, key name wrong, on one binding. The tool exists, is reachable and behaves correctly; only the string a permission rule / hook matcher must write is ours (`stopTask`, Pi's upstream tool name from `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:648`) instead of the documented one (`TaskStop`). Two of the three axes tools-reference.md:9 names are wrong (permission rules, hook matchers); the third (subagent tool lists) is already right via the alias table. Because `TaskStop` is absent from `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES` the mismatch is not merely silent: `managed-policy.ts:1034-1037` REFUSES any managed rule that raises `claude_rule.unknown_tool`, so an admin's `deny: ["TaskStop"]` is stripped from the policy entirely, and the Claude-settings importer (`permissions-config.ts:540`) installs a rule that matches nothing while logging the warning only to `debug()`. This is the same shape as the already-reasoned `Glob`→`Find` case (`claude-permission-rules.test.ts:245-247`), but with the opposite answer: `Find` is a deliberate product rename, whereas `stopTask` is the SAME tool under a non-documented spelling, and the file's own rule at `harness-tool-descriptor.ts:303-309` says the permissionName must be the documented spelling verbatim.

- **Документация связывает.** tools-reference.md:9 binds the fork to one spelling per tool: "The tool names are the exact strings you use in permission rules, subagent tool lists, and hook matchers", and its table (line 55) names the background-task stopper `TaskStop` (Permission required: No). permissions.md:158 states the consequence the finding quotes: "the tool labeled `Stop Task` in the transcript has the canonical name `TaskStop`. Permission rules and hook matchers match the canonical name only" — so `TaskStop` must be the string that a permission rule, a hook matcher and a subagent tool list all match, and the deny/ask unknown-tool startup warning must NOT fire for it.
  > For example, the tool labeled `Stop Task` in the transcript has the canonical name `TaskStop`. Permission rules and [hook matchers](/docs/en/hooks) match the canonical name only, so a rule written as `Stop Task` doesn't match.
- **У нас.** Our Pi harness spells the tool `stopTask` on every permission-visible axis. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:262` is `binding('stop_task', 'stop_task', 'stopTask', 'stopTask')` — the factory at :219-236 defaults `permissionName = handlerName`, so descriptorId/piName are `stop_task` and bindingName/handlerName/permissionName are `stopTask`. The three PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES consumers all pass the list unmapped — `permissions-config.ts:529` (Claude `settings.json` import), `managed-policy.ts:1017` (managed tier), `pi-agent.ts:3032` (hook-supplied `updatedPermissions`) — and no normalizer sits above them. The ONE place `TaskStop` already resolves is subagent/skill tool lists: `runtime-agent-definition.ts:94-95` carries `taskstop: ['stopTask','stop_task']` in `PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES`, consumed only by `normalizePiRuntimeAgentToolName` (:106-114). - **Пользователь.** Observable, but narrow and only on the Pi backend. Today a user who follows Claude's docs and puts `"deny": ["TaskStop"]` (or `"ask"`) in a `.claude/settings.json` we import gets a rule that installs and matches nothing: the tool is neither removed from the model's context nor gated, so the agent can still abort the user's background subagents and workflows despite the deny, and the mismatch warning goes only to `debug()` — there is no surfaced startup warning to catch it. On the managed/admin tier the failure is louder and the opposite direction: `managed-policy.ts:1034-1037` refuses any rule raising `claude_rule.unknown_tool`, so an administrator's `deny TaskStop` is stripped from the policy at load and reported as dropped. Third, a plugin or settings hook whose `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` matcher is `TaskStop` never fires on this tool, because the payload's `tool_name` is `stopTask`. Fourth and cosmetic: the transcript labels the call `stopTask`, a name that appears in no documentation the user can read. What makes it narrow is that nobody would guess `stopTask` on their own, so today the only way to write a working rule is to read our source — the documented spelling is the one that fails.

#### f121 · `auto-mode-config`

Not a key-name or value error: the sentinel string, the splice position semantics and the replace-on-absence semantics are all implemented correctly in `resolveAutoModeList`. What is missing is the operand — there are no built-in `environment`/`hard_deny`/`soft_deny`/`allow` lists in this fork to splice, and the sole production call site passes no `defaults`. Consequence in both documented directions: (1) including `"$defaults"` splices nothing, so a managed `['$defaults','x']` and a managed `['x']` produce byte-identical judge input, and the sentinel is silently swallowed with no drop record and no diagnostic; (2) omitting `"$defaults"` discards nothing, because the built-in taxonomy is unconditional prose in the judge's system prompt rather than one of the four addressable lists, so the Danger case at :212 is unreachable. The fork is therefore fail-safe on enforcement (no built-in protection is ever lost) and wrong on configuration (the documented splice is a no-op, and the documented take-full-ownership escape hatch does not exist).

- **Документация связывает.** auto-mode-config.md binds the literal string "$defaults" inside an `autoMode` array to a splice of the classifier's built-in rule list for that section: "To keep the built-in rules while adding your own, include the literal string `"$defaults"` in the array. The default rules are spliced in at that position, so your custom rules can go before or after them" (:182, and the same sentence for `environment` at :103). The Danger callout at :212 binds the inverse: "Setting any of `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, or `hard_deny` without `"$defaults"` replaces the entire default list for that section", naming the built-in soft blocks (force push, `curl | bash`, production deploys, auto-mode bypass) and the built-in `hard_deny` data-exfiltration rule as what is discarded. :218 adds that each of the four sections is evaluated independently.
  > To keep the built-in rules while adding your own, include the literal string `"$defaults"` in the array.
- **У нас.** The sentinel is a recognised constant and the splice primitive is correct, but nothing is ever spliced. `AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS_SENTINEL = '$defaults'` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:478) is consumed by `resolveAutoModeList` (:1061-1067), which flatMaps the sentinel to `[...defaults]` and returns `[...defaults]` for an absent list. `resolveAutoMode` (:1082-1101) declares `defaults: Partial<ResolvedAutoModePolicyV1> = {}` (:1089) and composes `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.managed?.[key], defaults[key] ?? [])` plus `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.user?.[key], [])` (:1092-1093). The ONLY production caller is packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4109, `resolveAutoMode({ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode })` — no second argument — so every `defaults[key]` is `[]` and the sentinel resolves to nothing. Live probe against the real modules: `resolveAutoMode({ managed: { soft_deny: ['$defaults','no hand migrations'] } })` and `resolveAutoMode({ managed: { soft_deny: ['no hand migrations'] } })` both return `{environment:[],hard_deny:[],soft_deny:['no hand migrations'],allow:[]}`, and `buildGuardianJudgeTask` produces a byte-identical task for the two (`task identical true`); the primitive itself works — `resolveAutoModeList(['a','$defaults','b'], ['D1'])` returns `['a','D1','b']`. The shipped test already pins the broken shape at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.test.ts:1025. No built-in rule list exists as data anywhere: an exhaustive `grep -a` for `soft_deny` over packages/apps/scripts/docs finds only the type declarations (managed-policy.ts:437, :464, guardian.ts:260), the parser (:850), the composer (:1098), the renderer (guardian.ts:346) and tests. Our built-in rules live instead as unconditional prose inside the judge's system prompt — `GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT` sections `## Data Exfiltration` / `## Credential Probing` / `## Persistent Security Weakening` / `## Destructive Actions` (packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:153-173) — installed as `systemPrompt: GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT` at packages/shared/src/agent/core/guardian-judge-core.ts:110 on every judge run, while the managed block only APPENDS a `## Organization policy` section to the task (guardian.ts:372, :382-383) and `describeOrgPolicy` returns `null` when all four resolved sets are empty (:342-349). The resolved value reaches the judge through the in-process `SessionCapabilityTurnRuntime.managedAutoMode` field (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:610), read at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3350-3353 where `hasAutoModePolicy` (managed-policy.ts:1110) drops it when every set is empty, and consumed at the two consult sites pi-agent.ts:3412/:3421 and :3516/:3527.
- **Пользователь.** For the documented add-your-own-rules case: none observable. An administrator who ships the page's example (`"soft_deny": ["$defaults", "Never run migrations outside the migrations CLI"]`) in the host-owned managed policy gets exactly the guardian behaviour they would get without the sentinel — verified by probe, the two produce a byte-identical judge task — and no protection is lost, because the built-in taxonomy is in the judge's system prompt regardless. The sentinel is dropped silently: the parser accepts it as ordinary prose (managed-policy.ts:837-847 records no drop), and there is no `claude auto-mode config`/`defaults` equivalent to inspect the effective list, so the admin has no surface that would reveal it. What IS observable is the take-full-ownership case the Danger callout describes: an admin who deliberately omits `"$defaults"` to drop a built-in rule — e.g. a team that force-pushes feature branches routinely and wants the built-in destructive-git soft block gone — still gets it applied, so in `auto` mode those pushes keep being routed to a human prompt with a guardian objection, and the only workaround is to add a counter-entry to `allow`. Latent today because the fork has no delivered managed policies in the wild that use the sentinel; it surfaces the moment one does.

The session-only trust mechanism EXISTS and works — `persistence: 'process-only'` keeps a decision in `ProjectTrustStore.processOnly` (project-trust-store.ts:101, :115-121, :149-152) and it expires with the process because the fingerprint is salted with a per-process random value (project-identity.ts:56, :118). The delta is that the home directory never reaches it: `persistence` is decided solely by stat success, so `$HOME` is classified `'stable'` and its grant is persisted. This is a missing one-branch carve-out in `resolveProjectIdentity`, not a missing mechanism and not a wrong field name. Second, smaller delta: even once the grant lapses, no surface re-prompts — `ProjectTrustDialog` is opened only from a directory-pick callback, never from a restored session whose project resolves `unknown`, so the doc's "the prompt reappears on each launch" leg needs its own edit.

- **Документация связывает.** glossary.md:231 (§ Project trust) binds project-trust acceptance to per-project-directory persistence with ONE exception: "Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch." The same line says what the grant buys — trust "gates auto-installation of marketplace plugins and execution of project-defined hooks" and makes the directory's `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json` and other config files take effect — so the home-directory carve-out is a security narrowing, not cosmetics.

- **У нас.** The fork treats $HOME as an ordinary project root and persists its grant like any other. (1) `ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory` is the sole raw-path ingress (packages/shared/src/projects/project-handle-service.ts:140-156) and it accepts $HOME: `validateCandidateProjectPath` (:250-274) rejects only non-absolute paths and managed paths, and `isManagedPath` (:276-278) matches only `CONFIG_DIR` plus injected managed workspace roots (:124-133). (2) `resolveProjectIdentity` returns `persistence: 'stable'` for any path the platform can stat — `process-only` is reached ONLY when `statIdentity` throws or reports `ino === 0n` (packages/shared/src/projects/project-identity.ts:116-133); there is no home-directory branch, and `grep -rain "homedir|process.env.HOME" packages/shared/src/projects packages/shared/src/capabilities` returns nothing (exit 1). (3) `ProjectTrustStore.record` therefore writes the home grant to `CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-trust-store.ts:135-158) and `resolve` reads it back for any `'stable'` identity (:114-128), so the grant survives a restart. (4) Nothing upstream carves home out either: the RPC `projects.SET_TRUST` handler passes the ref straight through (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/projects.ts:78-86), `SessionManager.setProjectTrust` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14537-14613) has no path special-case, and the renderer opens `ProjectTrustDialog` purely on `trustState === 'unknown'` at pick time (apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/ChatPage.tsx:339-341, apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/settings/WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx:251). (5) The grant is material: project-scope instruction/skill/agent/MCP/hook/permission records are emitted only when `context.projectTrustState === 'trusted'` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:995-1024), project `.nessy-agent/config.toml` defaults load only when trusted (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:8878-8880), the trusted-project plugin policy overlay requires it (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:951), and `isPiLspProvisioningAllowed` requires it (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2090-2091).
- **Пользователь.** Concrete and security-relevant. Pick your home folder as a session's project folder or as a workspace default project (Chat working-directory picker, or Settings → Workspace → Default project folder), click Trust once in the dialog, and the grant is written to disk forever: every later launch silently loads and executes everything project-scope under the whole home tree — `~/.nessy-agent/hooks.json` hook commands, `~/.nessy-agent/mcp.json` servers, project skills/agents/permissions (native-sources.ts:995-1024), project `.nessy-agent/config.toml` defaults, and Pi LSP provisioning — with no re-prompt. In Claude Code that same click lasts one session and the dialog comes back next launch. Because the home tree is where every unrelated repo, download and cache lives, this is the one directory where a persisted grant has effectively unbounded reach. The user sees nothing to tell them apart: the dialog and the trusted badge look identical to a normal project's.

Two deltas, and the first is polarity, not naming. (1) Inverted default: with no flags, upstream keeps a resumable session and we hard-delete it; the same command produces opposite outcomes. (2) The opt-in is inverted with it and spelled differently — ours is `--no-cleanup` meaning "keep", the doc's is `--no-session-persistence` meaning "discard" — and the discard MECHANISM differs too: the doc says such sessions "are not saved to disk" (never written, which is exactly our existing `ephemeral: true`), whereas we write the record and then remove it durably. Missing alongside: the `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` env equivalent that upstream honours "in any mode". Not covered by the row but worth stating so nobody thinks the flag alone closes it: `run` never prints the session id, so a kept session has no user-visible handle.

Print mode only. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` environment variable does the same in any mode" — i.e. never-written, not written-then-removed.

#### f175 · `goal`

Not a key-name or value mismatch — a missing state transition plus a validator that forbids it.

(a) On `parsed.complete === true` we write verdict `complete_suggested` and keep `status: 'active'` (goal-service.ts:248-259) where the page requires clearing the goal and recording an achieved entry. The correct enum value already exists in every schema (`completed` / `status: 'complete'`), so no wire type changes; only which value the evaluator branch produces.
(b) Even if (a) were flipped, `validTerminalState` (:555) would reject the record on reload because it demands `evaluation.source === 'manual'`. So the fix is two edits in one file, not one line.
(c) The evidence invariant the page implies is already satisfied on the evaluator path: `parseEvaluatorResult` calls `evidenceList(record.evidence, record.complete)` (:498), so `complete: true` with empty evidence is already downgraded to `not_complete` (locked by goal-service.test.ts:154-155). Nothing new is needed there.
(d) The "records an achieved entry in the transcript" half is entirely absent — no transcript/receipt entry and no `['goal']` domain invalidation is emitted when a goal terminates.
(e) Wider than filed: the page's whole premise (the USER types a condition, a FRESH model decides completion) has no surface here. There is no `/goal`, no `/goal clear`, no status view; only the model can create a goal, and only the model can complete it — the loop is model-owned end to end.
(f) Narrower than filed in one respect, and this is a deliberate superset, not a defect: our extra spend is capped by budgets (goal-service.ts:14-19, :284) where Claude's `/goal` is uncapped. Keep it.
(g) Cosmetic only: `MAX_CONDITION` is 8_192 (goal-service.ts:21) against the documented 4,000-character limit (:72) — more permissive, no user-visible divergence.

- **Документация связывает.** goal.md:129 binds the post-turn evaluator's yes to a terminal outcome: "**Yes**: Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript." Reinforced at :13 ("The goal clears automatically once the condition is met") and in the comparison table at :28 (`/goal` — "Stops when: A model confirms the condition is met"). The page also binds a user entry point — `/goal <condition>` sets it (:42-52), `/goal clear` removes it (:98), bare `/goal` shows condition, elapsed, turns evaluated, token spend and the evaluator's most recent reason (:78-94) — and states that completion is "decided by a fresh model rather than the one doing the work" (:34).
  > **Yes**: Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript.
- **У нас.** The mechanism exists as a Pi-harness session goal service with a post-settlement evaluator and an auto-continuation loop, but the evaluator has no terminal authority and there is no user surface.

1. On a yes, the goal stays active. `GoalService.evaluateAtSettlement` commits at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.ts:248-259 by spreading `...current`, so `status` remains `'active'`; it only writes `lastEvaluation: evaluation('evaluator', parsed.complete ? 'complete_suggested' : 'not_complete', ...)` (:252-258).
2. Only a manual command can terminate. `terminalGoal` (goal-service.ts:343-359) has exactly two callers, both in the same file: `action === 'complete'` (:151-155) and `action === 'cancel'` (:157-159). `terminalGoal` hardcodes `evaluation('manual', ...)` at :357.
3. The persistence validator structurally forbids an evaluator-sourced completion: `validTerminalState` (goal-service.ts:551-561) requires, for `status === 'complete'`, `evaluation.source === 'manual' && evaluation.verdict === 'completed' && evaluation.evidence.length > 0` (:555).
4. The evaluator is told it is advisory: `evaluatorPrompt` emits "Advisory goal check only. You have no tools and cannot change goal state." (goal-service.ts:480).
5. The consequence is a real extra turn. `SessionManager.schedulePiGoalContinuation` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3360-3411) awaits `evaluateAtSettlement` at :3376 (evaluator model = `managed.agent.runMiniCompletion`, :3379), re-reads `service.safeSnapshot()` at :3383 and gates only on `status !== 'active'`; `canContinue` (goal-service.ts:264-271) checks settled + active + id/revision match and never inspects the verdict, so the fresh post-evaluation revision matches and :3398 dispatches another full turn via `sendMessage`. The only nudge is textual: `continuationPrompt` (goal-service.ts:273-282) appends `Last evaluation: complete_suggested: <reason>` and "Use Goal complete only with concrete evidence".
6. `complete_suggested` has zero consumers. `grep -ran complete_suggested apps packages` finds it only at the producer (goal-service.ts:254), three type/parser allowlists (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:114, packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:139, packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:106, goal-service.ts:608) and one test that LOCKS the behaviour (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.test.ts:146, in the case named "runs the advisory evaluator only when settled and never grants terminal authority", :128-146).
7. No user surface exists. `grep -ran goal_create apps packages` finds the action only in the wire type (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:346), its parser (packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:295) and the SessionManager control arm (SessionManager.ts:3279-3285, which does stamp `source: 'user', creator: 'desktop'`); no renderer sends it. The only shipped producer is the pi-only `Goal` tool (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:991, description :644) whose port hardcodes `source: 'agent', creator: 'pi'` (SessionManager.ts:12148-12156). `PiHarnessRuntimeSnapshotV1.goal` (core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:308) and the `'goal'` invalidation domain (:12) exist but nothing in apps/electron/src/renderer or packages/ui reads them — the only renderer files matching "goal" are unrelated turn-card prose (packages/ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:310).
8. Ours bounds the loop where Claude's does not: `DEFAULT_PI_GOAL_BUDGETS` (goal-service.ts:14-19) caps a goal at 32 turns / 250k tokens / $20 / 2h and `enforceBudgetsLocked` (:284-294) terminates it as `budget_exhausted`.
- **Пользователь.** Pi sessions only, and only after the model has set a goal with the pi-only `Goal` tool — there is no way for a user to set one. When it happens: the evaluator says the condition is met and the session KEEPS WORKING. SessionManager dispatches another full billed turn shown as "Continue active goal (<id>@<rev>)" (SessionManager.ts:3388, :3398), carrying `Last evaluation: complete_suggested: <reason>` in the prompt, and keeps dispatching after every settlement until the model itself calls `Goal complete` or a budget trips. So a goal whose work is demonstrably finished can burn turns up to 32 turns / 250k tokens / $20 / 2h and then end as `budget_exhausted` rather than complete — a successful goal recorded as a budget failure. The user has no way to see or stop this short of stopping the session: no `/goal` command, no status view, no achieved entry in the transcript, and no UI reads `PiHarnessRuntimeSnapshotV1.goal`. What they experience is an agent that will not stop and a chat that keeps producing turns with no visible reason. Whether it surfaces at all depends on the model volunteering `Goal complete` promptly — in the common case it costs one extra turn, in the bad case it costs the whole budget.

#### f154 · `deep-links`

Two deltas, both on the execution half of the page; the directory half already complies. (1) EXECUTION: an OS/web-delivered link is not inert. `send=true` reaches `sendMessage` with no user step (NavigationContext.tsx:753-764), and six further cases in the same switch mutate state (delete-session, delete-source, rename, flag/unflag, set-mode, oauth). The doc's handler accepts one path, `open`; ours accepts any `action/<name>` the switch knows. This is not a wrong key name — the value is honoured and the effect is real. (2) DISCLOSURE: no `Prompt from an external link` warning line exists in any form, so even the non-send prefill path (`onInputChange`) gives the user no signal that the text came from a link, and there is no >1,000-char review notice. Structurally, the missing primitive is an origin distinction: `handleDeepLink` and the `DeepLinkNavigation` DTO carry no `origin`, so the renderer cannot tell an in-app dispatch (EditPopover.tsx:1089, which legitimately needs `send=true`) from an OS or web-page URL. Also out of spec but harmless: the prompt param is `input`, not `q`, and there is no 5,000-char cap.

- **Документация связывает.** deep-links.md:39 binds an OS-delivered link to being inert: "A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box." — nothing reaches the model until the user reads what was filled in and presses Enter. deep-links.md:45 binds the handler's surface: `claude-cli://open` is "the only path the handler accepts", carrying only `q` (prompt prefill, max 5,000 chars), `cwd` and `repo`. deep-links.md:41 binds the disclosure: when the session opens, "a warning line below the input box reads `Prompt from an external link` and stays visible until you send or clear the prompt", with a character count and a scroll-and-review instruction for prompts over 1,000 characters.

A markdown link in an assistant message also reaches it: packages/ui/src/components/markdown/Markdown.tsx:201-224 hands the ORIGINAL href to `onUrlClick` (only the DOM `href` attribute is stripped), which lands on RPC `shell.OPEN_URL` at apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:206-223 where `classifyExternalUrl` returns `internal-deeplink` (packages/shared/src/utils/url-safety.ts:54-55) and :220 calls `handleDeepLink` — the `dangerous` gate at :209-212 never fires for `nessy:`. `parseDeepLink` copies every query param except `window` and `sidebar` into `actionParams` (apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:159-164 for the workspace form, :185-190 for `nessy://action/...`), so `send`, `mode`, `model`, `systemPrompt`, `badges`, `status`, `label` all survive. `handleDeepLink` (:235-342) pushes a `DeepLinkNavigation` on `deeplink:navigate` at :334-338 with no origin field (the DTO has none: packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:992-998). - **Пользователь.** Live and severe today, on three surfaces. A `nessy://action/new-session?input=<attacker text>&send=true` link — on any web page, in a Slack/wiki message, in a page opened in Nessy's own browser pane, or rendered as a markdown link inside an assistant message — creates a session on one click and sends the attacker's prompt to the model roughly 100 ms later. The user sees a new chat appear with a message they did not write, already being answered; there is no confirmation, no `Prompt from an external link` warning, and nothing to cancel before the turn starts. The same link can set the new session's permission mode, and `parsePermissionMode` accepts `bypassPermissions` (also spelled `allowall` or `execute`), so the auto-sent prompt can run in the mode that does not ask before tool use. Sibling links are destructive without any prompt at all: `nessy://action/delete-session/<id>` deletes a session, `nessy://action/delete-source/<id>` removes a source, `nessy://action/set-mode/<sessionId>?mode=bypassPermissions` flips an existing session out of its permission mode, and `nessy://action/oauth/<sourceSlug>` starts a sign-in flow. Session ids are guessable enough for a shotgun link, and the markdown-link surface means model output that quotes a fetched web page is itself a delivery path. Nothing in the UI distinguishes any of this from a link the user's own app generated.

#### f104 · `context-window`

Two separate deltas, neither of them a naming or value mismatch.
(1) The 25KB limit is absent in every form — no constant, no check, on either path. Not a wrong key, not a wrong value: nothing implements the byte dimension.
(2) The 200-line limit is implemented with the correct value (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`) but only inside `readMemoryFile`, which `system.ts:453-455` bypasses whenever a capability runtime exists — i.e. on every turn of both shipping backends. On the path that actually feeds the model, `base-agent.ts:976-1014`, neither limit is applied, so a MEMORY.md of arbitrary size enters context whole. Observable production behaviour is therefore 'no cap', which contradicts the page rather than narrowing it; the correct-valued cap sitting on the dead branch is why this reads as partial from the constant alone.

- **Документация связывает.** context-window.md:29, the `Auto memory (MEMORY.md)` entry of the ContextWindow EVENTS array: "The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context." MEMORY.md content that enters the conversation context must therefore be truncated at min(200 lines, 25KB) — two limits, whichever binds first. #### f176 · `headless`

The value, not the mechanism: SIGTERM must exit 143 and exits 130. Both signals share one handler with a constant exit code, so a supervisor cannot distinguish an operator Ctrl-C from an infrastructure shutdown. SIGINT's 130 is already correct and must stay. Registering ANY handler is what breaks it — Node/Bun's default SIGTERM disposition already yields 143; the explicit `process.exit(130)` overwrites the correct number. Positive control on this rig, both runtimes: a script using our exact pattern exits 130 on SIGTERM, the same script with the two `process.on` lines removed exits 143 (node 130/143, bun 130/143). The sentence's other three clauses (abort the turn, terminate the Bash process tree via the server teardown, run SessionEnd) are already satisfied through the cancel + child-SIGTERM path above and are NOT part of this divergence.

- **Документация связывает.** headless.md:69 (§ Background tasks at exit) binds the non-interactive run's exit status to the signal that stopped it: "If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs `SessionEnd` hooks, and exits with code 143." 143 is the 128+SIGTERM convention, i.e. distinct from the 130 that a SIGINT (128+2) interrupt produces.
  > If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs [`SessionEnd` hooks](/docs/en/hooks#sessionend), and exits with code 143.
- **У нас.** `nessy-general-agent run` is our `claude -p` analogue (`cmdRun`, apps/cli/src/index.ts:764; print mode declared at apps/cli/src/index.ts:782 via `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })`). It registers ONE handler for both signals and hard-codes a single exit code: `const onSignal = async () => { ... await cleanup(); process.exit(130) }` at apps/cli/src/index.ts:796-802, with `process.on('SIGINT', onSignal)` at :803 and `process.on('SIGTERM', onSignal)` at :804 (torn down at :861-862). The handler does perform the other clauses of the sentence: it cancels the turn (`client.invoke('sessions:cancel', sessionId)`, apps/cli/src/index.ts:798) and then `cleanup()` (:787-793) SIGTERMs the spawned headless server (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:118-121), whose own `shutdown` (packages/server/src/index.ts:367-374) runs `instance.stop()` -> `cleanupSessionManager` (packages/server/src/index.ts:270-277) -> `SessionManager.cleanup()` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:19138), where SessionEnd is run per managed session (SessionManager.ts:19160-19164). Only the exit number is wrong. `process.exit(130)` occurs exactly once in the whole source tree (`grep -ran 'process.exit(130)\|process.exit(143)' apps packages scripts` -> apps/cli/src/index.ts:801 only), and no test asserts a signal exit code (`grep -an 'SIGTERM|SIGINT|130|143' apps/cli/src/run.test.ts` -> no hits). Our own reference documents only the stream-event codes and has no signal row: docs/cli.md:131-133 (`error` 1, `complete` 0, `interrupted` 130).
- **Пользователь.** Observable today, on the first SIGTERM. Anyone running `nessy-general-agent run <prompt>` under a supervisor — `kill`, `systemd` stop, `docker stop`, a Kubernetes pod eviction, a GitLab CI job cancel or timeout, or an SDK host closing the session — gets exit status 130 instead of 143. Two concrete consequences: a wrapper written to the near-universal SIGTERM convention (`if [ $? -eq 143 ]`, or shell `$((128+15))`) never matches, so an infrastructure-initiated shutdown is reported as a generic failure; and a pipeline that treats 130 as 'the operator cancelled, do not alert' silently swallows a real timeout kill or eviction, because our 130 now means SIGINT, SIGTERM and the streamed `interrupted` event all at once. SIGINT/Ctrl-C behaviour is correct and unaffected.
