Two separable deltas, both on the settings-parse boundary; the enforcement half is correct and untouched. (a) KEY NAME AND NESTING. Three of the doc's four path keys are spelled differently and live one level up: `filesystem.allowWrite` -> `additionalWritableRoots`, `filesystem.denyWrite` -> `deniedWriteRoots`, `filesystem.denyRead` -> `deniedReadRoots`. The VALUES, the merge semantics and the enforcement are right — allowWrite/additionalWritableRoots grants and concatenates, the two deny lists restrict and ride the floor, and the resolved lists reach the OS profile correctly. Only the accepted spelling is wrong, which is why the fix is an accepted-alias widening and not a rewrite. `filesystem.allowRead` and `filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly` and `filesystem.disabled` are already correct, so the object is half-conformant, which is what makes the rejection surprising. (b) PATH PREFIXES. The sentence the finding quotes is about prefixes, and none of the three non-absolute prefixes is implemented for ANY of these keys, including the two whose names are already right: `~/` is not expanded, `./` and bare are not resolved against a scope root, and `//abs` is accepted but never normalized to `/abs`. So even a user who translates the key names by hand cannot write `~/.aws/credentials` or `.`, the doc's own examples. Consequence differs by tier and neither is an app failure: at USER scope the strict parse throws and `getUserSandboxSettings` (storage.ts:1293) catches it, logs "[settings] Invalid `sandbox` in the user config — the layer is rejected whole and ignored" (storage.ts:1239) and returns `{}` — the whole `sandbox` layer is inert while the rest of `config.json` applies; at MANAGED scope nothing throws and the tolerant sink strips PER KEY, so `excludedCommands` and `network` still apply while the write/read boundary silently disappears. The URL, method and header values are all correct; the delta is one absent `RequestInit` field at each of two call sites. We follow redirects where the page requires a redirect to be a failure, so a 30x from the gateway (or from a TLS-terminating proxy in front of it) forwards the gateway JWT / API key to a third host instead of aborting discovery. This is not a key-name mismatch and not a response-parsing difference. Secondary delta from the same doc sentence: the documented 3-second request timeout has no counterpart — nestor.ts:41 has no timeout, and drivers/anthropic.ts ignores the `timeoutMs` it receives. Explicitly NOT a divergence: the rest of the documented request shape (`/v1/models`, `limit=1000`, the `data[]` envelope, the claude/anthropic id-prefix filter) does not transfer to the Nestor path — that endpoint is Nessy's own corporate REST route `/api/v1/cli/models` returning a bare `NestorModel[]` (nestor.ts:10,22-31,49), by design; only the no-redirect hardening transfers.

- **Документация связывает.** llm-gateway-protocol.md:157 binds a gateway model-discovery request to a no-redirect transport: "The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target." The same line's second sentence states the intent — "A gateway that responds slowly or redirects `/v1/models`, even `http` to `https`, fails discovery silently; serve the endpoint directly at the configured base URL." So: a 3xx on the model-list endpoint must abort discovery, never be followed, and the credential header must reach only the configured base URL.

#### f009 · `hooks`

Not a key-name problem and not a wrong value: the hooks subsystem is never handed the effort at all. Three separate absences behind one doc sentence.

1. INPUT FIELD ABSENT. `effort` is not on `SdkAutomationInput` (types.ts:742-901), so `effort.level` cannot appear on hook stdin or in `NESSY_EVENT_DATA`. Note the documented shape is an OBJECT with a `level` field, not a bare string — a fix that sets `effort: "high"` would satisfy a grep and still break `jq -r '.effort.level'`.

2. ENV VAR ABSENT FOR HOOKS. `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46-81) mirrors a closed list of fourteen fields and would not emit an effort variable even once the input carries one. The documented spelling is `CLAUDE_EFFORT`; this builder emits no `CLAUDE_*` key of its own today (Claude-spelled keys reach a hook only through `actionEnv` from `claudeCompatPluginEnv`, data-paths.ts:127-135), so this is also the first host-owned Claude-spelled variable it would produce. The fork's own precedent for that is the skills path, which emits BOTH spellings (runtime-skill-content.ts:136).

3. ENV VAR ABSENT FOR THE BASH TOOL. The doc's second clause ("and the Bash tool") has no implementation on either bash surface (pi-agent.ts:5191-5212, local-tools/runtime.ts:520). This half is independent of 1 and 2 — it is not fixed by fixing the hook input.

One thing is NOT divergent and must not be "fixed": the exec-form placeholder list (hook-command.ts:161-170) is deliberately closed to documented PATH placeholders. hooks.md:637 calls `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` an environment variable, not an exec-form placeholder, and exec form documents that `$`-forms pass through verbatim, so `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` staying literal in an `args` element is correct behaviour.

Same for a Bash tool call: `echo $CLAUDE_EFFORT` in any command the model runs prints empty.

It surfaces the moment someone follows hooks-guide.md § *Stop hook hits the block cap* — which is exactly the audience that hits it, since the doc prescribes the variable as the remedy for a hook that legitimately needs more than eight iterations. That user exports `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP=20`, restarts Nessy, and nothing changes: from the 9th consecutive block onward their Stop (or SubagentStop) hook's `reason` silently stops reaching the model, so the agent stops being told what still needs doing and the convergence loop the hook was driving stalls one iteration short. There is no UI signal at all — the suppression writes only `this.debug(...)` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:565), which lands in logs, not in the chat surface, so the symptom the user sees is "my hook stopped having any effect" with no explanation. `0` (disable the cap) is equally inert.

Note the fork's cap suppresses re-delivery of the reason rather than force-ending a continued turn (deliberate — packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:550-553; we cannot re-run a finished turn), so the symptom differs in shape from Claude's "turn ends with a warning", but the trigger point and the missing knob are the same.

The one adjacent behaviour that DOES exist — `ensureBackgroundFetch` re-cloning a stale catalog off the request path — is browse-triggered rather than scheduled and updates catalog metadata only, so it is not a narrower version of the documented behaviour but a different one. A user who installs a plugin from a marketplace never learns a newer version exists: the plugin row's Update action is permanently unavailable because `canUpdate` is computed from a field nothing ever writes (views.ts:443 over resolver input storage-runtime.ts:826), so the only way to get a new version is to notice by hand, click the per-registry Upgrade button on the Plugins page to re-clone the catalog, then click the plugin's Repair — and the repair path re-stages the same version anyway unless the catalog moved. Plugins therefore sit at their install-time version indefinitely, including through upstream security fixes. Second, an administrator who writes `"autoUpdate": true` on an `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry from Claude's page gets nothing and is told nothing: the key is dropped before the managed-policy drop sink sees it, so it appears in neither config-doctor output nor the managed-drop report, and the marketplace behaves exactly as if the key were absent. There is no auto-update toggle anywhere in the plugin manager UI, so a user following the documented four-step path finds no such control.

#### f047 · `discover-plugins`

Not a wrong key name or a narrower value — the whole three-part mechanism is absent: the entry field is deliberately dropped, the managed key is not in the schema (and is actively rejected as unknown), and there is no Discover-tab pin or annotation to receive a match. One further gap is structural rather than merely missing code: settings.md:302 allowlists by marketplace NAME, and Nessy persists no marketplace name. `PluginMarketplaceRegistry` (packages/shared/src/plugins/store.ts:42-62) stores `id`, `source`, `refName`, `displayName`; the catalog's own `name` (`ExternalPluginCatalogDto.name`, external-catalog-adapters.ts:55) is parsed and never stored. A delivered marketplace is the only case with a real name today, because `deliverMarketplaces` passes `displayName: entry.name` from the managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` key (registry-source.ts:358-362); a user-added registry's `displayName` is derived from its source string (`registryDisplayName` :952-954). The doc's own source-correspondence rule happens to cover the delivered case exactly, so the name identity gap only bites for a marketplace allowlisted by name whose source is declared through `strictKnownMarketplaces` instead.

#### f054 · `plugins-reference`

The whole mechanism is missing, not a key name or a value. Three separable deltas. (a) Discovery: no scanner ever stats `<skills-dir>/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; `skillRecords` gates on `SKILL.md` alone (`native-sources.ts:282`), so a doc-conformant bundle — which per `:383` puts its skills at `<folder>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and need carry no root `SKILL.md` — contributes NOTHING. Only the subset that happens to also carry a root `SKILL.md` degrades to a bare skill with its agents/hooks/MCP silently dropped; the filed prose asserted that degraded case universally, which overstates one shape and understates the other. (b) Loading model: the doc's plugin is discovered in place and never enters the cache (`:376`), and has no uninstall because nothing was installed (`:409`); our only representation of a plugin is a cache-resident `PluginInstalledEntryV2` with a required `cacheRef` (`store-v2.ts:48`) placed by `install()` (`store-v2.ts:198`-`:200`). (c) Identity and control: `skills-dir` exists in neither `PluginOriginSource` (`plugins/types.ts:35`) nor the managed marketplace-source classifier (`managed-marketplace-entries.ts:170`-`:206`), so the key `<name>@skills-dir` cannot be produced and the documented `{"source": "skills-dir"}` admin switch is parsed as invalid and dropped. Also missing but subordinate: `/reload-plugins`, `plugin init`, and a `plugin disable` verb. Note the two roots the doc names (`~/.claude/skills/`, `<cwd>/.claude/skills/`) are not scanned at all in the fork under any name — the equivalent roots we do scan are `~/.agents/skills` and `<cwd>/.agents/skills` — so this is not a rebrand-path difference: the mechanism is absent whatever the directory is called.

Scaffold one with `plugin init`. Unlike a marketplace install, the plugin is discovered in place rather than copied into the plugin cache." The disambiguation table fixes the three cases — `:382` `<skills-dir>/foo/SKILL.md` with no manifest is "A plain skill named `foo`"; `:383` `<skills-dir>/foo/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is "A plugin `foo@skills-dir`, which can bundle its own skills, agents, hooks, and more". The scope table fixes exactly two roots: `:390` `~/.claude/skills/` = personal, loads "In every project"; `:391` `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` = project, "Only after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder", with `:395` requiring its MCP servers to go through "the same per-server approval as a project `.mcp.json`". `:402` forbids the ancestor walk for these specifically: they "load only from the `.claude/skills/` of the directory where you start Claude Code. - **У нас.** The fork has no in-place plugin discovery of any kind; every plugin must be resolved through an install that stages a copy into the content-addressed plugin cache. - **Пользователь.** A user who follows Claude's own docs and drops a plugin folder into a skills directory gets total silence. The nearest shipped behaviour — install from a URL or local path — is the opposite of the documented one: it writes an installed record, so it violates plugins/cli-reference.md#flags-that-load-a-plugin-for-one-session (was line 1096 of the retired plugins-reference page) ("no installed record") and plugins.md:344 ("that session only"), and it offers no name-override-for-this-session semantics (plugins.md:328). #### f037 · `agent-sdk/mcp`

The transport itself is fully implemented — we speak streamable HTTP, under the name `http`, with the correct typed value in `SdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:733-735). The delta is exactly one accepted spelling at the JSON parse boundary: the documented alias `"streamable-http"` is not mapped to `"http"`. It is a key-value-name gap, not a missing capability, and the doc's third sentence means the fix must be a fold-at-parse (emit `'http'`), never a widening of the transport union. Second-order: our rejection is also quieter than a rejection should be — `parseMcpServersDocument`'s warning goes to an optional `debug` callback that defaults to a no-op (runtime-pool-servers.ts:273 `const debug = options.debug ?? (() => {})`), while the entry still appears in the capability inventory, so the user sees a listed server with no tools and no message.

- **Документация связывает.** `agent-sdk/mcp.md:375` binds the JSON configuration surface: "For the streamable HTTP transport, use `"type": "http"` instead. In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"`. The programmatic `mcpServers` option accepts only `"http"`." So every JSON reader of an MCP server map must treat `"streamable-http"` as `"http"`, and the alias must be folded away at parse time — the programmatic/typed `mcpServers` value stays `"http"`-only, so the transport union must NOT be widened.

- **Пользователь.** Concrete and silent. Many MCP servers document their own JSON as `"type": "streamable-http"`, because that is the MCP specification's name for the transport. A user who pastes that block into `.mcp.json`, `~/.nessy/mcp.json` or `.nessy-agent/mcp.json` gets a server that never connects and exposes no tools. It is not simply missing from the UI: the capability inventory keys off the server name regardless of `type` (native-sources.ts:493-503), and with `transport` unset but `url` present the panel labels it `http` via the fallback at resolver.ts:1653 — so the MCP/Sources surface lists an apparently-normal HTTP server that produces nothing. The only trace is `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config`, routed to a `debug` callback that defaults to a no-op (runtime-pool-servers.ts:273), so with no debug sink attached there is no message at all. The user's next move is to suspect their token or the server. Same for plugin install: a Claude plugin bundling a `.mcp.json` with that spelling imports with the server missing and the diagnostic `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).`, which is misleading — the entry does have a `url`.

#### f040 · `mcp`

The entire client-side roots surface is missing — this is not a wrong key name or a narrowed value. Three distinct absences: the `roots` client capability (with `listChanged: true`) is never declared at the MCP handshake; no `roots/list` request handler is registered, so the method does not exist on our client; `notifications/roots/list_changed` is never emitted. The data the doc says to answer with is already computed and correct in this repo (workspace root + `additionalDirectories` + session `addDirectories` grants) — it simply has no path to the MCP wire. Secondary structural delta: Claude Code has one MCP client per session, so its roots are per-session; Nessy's pool is shared per (workspaceId, projectKey) and leased by sessions (workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:165-166, :201-230), so one connection cannot answer differently per session — a decision the implementation must make explicitly rather than inherit.

- **Документация связывает.** mcp.md:108 binds the client side of MCP roots: "Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every additional working directory you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting" and "Claude Code sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes." The preceding sentence makes this the designated mechanism rather than an extra: "A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP `roots/list` request instead" (instead of reading `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`). So our MCP client must declare the `roots` capability with `listChanged`, serve `roots/list` with launch dir + additional working directories, and emit `notifications/roots/list_changed` on every change to that set.
  > Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting.
- **У нас.** Nessy never exposes MCP roots to any server, on any transport, for any backend. (1) Capability: packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 constructs `new Client({name:'nessy-agent',version:'1.0.0'}, { capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {} })` — the capabilities value is an either/or ternary with no accumulator, and `roots` appears in neither branch. (2) Handler: the only request handler registered on that client is `ElicitRequestSchema` (client.ts:325-343); the notification handlers are elicitation-complete plus tools/resources/prompts list-changed (client.ts:346-360). No `ListRootsRequestSchema` handler exists, so a server that sent `roots/list` anyway would get 'Method not found'. (3) Notification: `sendRootsListChanged` is never called. (4) Absence is repo-wide and NUL-safe: `grep -ran "roots/list\|ListRootsRequestSchema\|listRoots\|sendRootsListChanged\|RootsListChanged" packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` exits 1 with zero hits. (5) Nothing adds it later — the repo's only `registerCapabilities` is `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/capabilities.ts:89`, an unrelated RPC-handler registrar in a sibling subsystem, not an MCP capability registration. (6) The two sibling MCP clients omit roots too: packages/shared/src/mcp/api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument; packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:411-413 passes `{ capabilities: {} }`. (7) The consequence reaches every backend because Nessy's own pool is the sole client that connects third-party servers: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1136 builds each `NessyMcpClient` with only `elicitationHandler`/`channelServer`/`pluginProcessAuthority`, and packages/shared/src/mcp/pool-server.ts:210-213 re-exposes that same pool to Pi/Codex as a SERVER (`nessy-pool-proxy`, `capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true } }`), so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path. (8) The SDK is ready and asserts on our omission: node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/index.js:621 exposes `sendRootsListChanged()`, :394 throws unless `_capabilities.roots.listChanged` is set, :427 throws unless `_capabilities.roots` is set. (9) Both inputs the doc names already exist server-side of us: the launch-directory analogue is the pool's `workspaceRootPath` (mcp-pool.ts:578, :643, :685; resolved at packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:245 and passed at :790), and the additional-directory list is the persisted `additionalDirectories` setting (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:132, packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:191 and :227) canonicalized into a `roots: string[]` by packages/shared/src/agent/additional-directories.ts (`resolveAdditionalDirectories`, `getConfiguredAdditionalDirectories`), already unioned with the session-scoped `addDirectories` grant by packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2711-2717 over packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3193-3212. (10) The current capability surface is pinned by test: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:79-90 asserts `sdkClient._capabilities.elicitation` equals `{form:{},url:{}}` with a handler and that the capabilities object is otherwise empty without one.
- **Пользователь.** Latent for most users today, and concretely broken for one class of server. A user connects an MCP server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots (the pattern mcp.md:108 explicitly routes servers to): the server's `initialize` response shows a client with no `roots` capability, so it never asks, falls back to its own default — typically nothing, or an operator-configured allowlist — and its file tools then either refuse ('no accessible roots' / 'path not allowed') or operate on the wrong directory. In the Sources surface such a server connects and lists tools normally, so nothing looks wrong; the failure appears only when a tool is called. Second, invisible-by-construction effect: a user who adds a working directory mid-session (the `addDirectories` grant path, pi-agent.ts:3193) or edits `additionalDirectories` in settings gets no `notifications/roots/list_changed`, so even a server that had roots would keep the stale set for the life of the connection. What would make it surface broadly: any commonly installed server adopting roots-based scoping — the mechanism is client-advertised, so adoption on the server side alone turns this from latent into a visible tool failure with no diagnostic pointing at us.
- **Правка.**
  - `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts` `NessyMcpClient constructor + PoolClient` — Add constructor option `rootsProvider?: () => readonly string[] | Promise<readonly string[]>`. Rewrite the capabilities argument at :310-324 from the either/or ternary into an accumulated object — `{ ...(options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}), ...(options?.rootsProvider ? { roots: { listChanged: true } } : {}) }` — because a naive key append to the current ternary would drop elicitation in one branch. When `rootsProvider` is present, register `this.client.setRequestHandler(ListRootsRequestSchema, async () => ({ roots: (await provider()).map(p => ({ uri: pathToFileURL(p).href, name: basename(p) })) }))` (import `ListRootsRequestSchema` from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js', `pathToFileURL` from 'node:url'); the MCP `Root.uri` must be a `file://` URI, not a bare path. Add a public `async notifyRootsChanged(): Promise<void>` that no-ops unless connected and the capability was declared, then calls `this.client.sendRootsListChanged()` (the SDK throws otherwise — dist/esm/client/index.js:394). Add `notifyRootsChanged?(): Promise<void>` as an OPTIONAL member of the `PoolClient` interface at :234-255 so `ApiSourcePoolClient` (in-process API sources, which need no roots) stays conformant unchanged.
  - `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts` `McpClientPool constructor options + connect() + a new notifyRootsChanged()` — Add `rootsProvider?: () => readonly string[] | Promise<readonly string[]>` to the options bag at :641-683 (next to `workspaceRootPath` at :643) and store it at :685. Pass it through at :1136 into `new NessyMcpClient(clientConfig, { ... })`. #### f062 · `skills`

Not a key-name or value mismatch — the field names and accepted values match the page exactly; there is simply no consumer. A skill declaring `context: fork` runs INLINE in the main conversation with full history, instead of as an isolated subagent whose prompt is the SKILL.md content, and its result never arrives as a separate background completion. `background` is inert because its governing field is; `agent` is honoured but re-purposed as a per-turn agent ceiling rather than skills.md:270's fork target; `hooks` has no per-component lifecycle scope; `shell` has no interpreter to select because inline `` !`command` `` execution does not exist in skill bodies at all (so validation.ts:250's stated reason is itself inaccurate). The delta is a missing isolation guarantee, not an inverted one: dropping `context` yields exactly the behaviour a fieldless skill gets.

- **Документация связывает.** skills.md:547 binds `context: fork` to isolation: "Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history." Three frontmatter fields depend on it and are specified in the same reference table: `agent` (:270) "Which subagent type to use when `context: fork` is set"; `background` (:271) "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait for the forked subagent's result in the turn that invoked the skill, instead of running it in the background. Default: `true`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later"; and independently `hooks` (:272) "Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle" and `shell` (:274) "Shell to use for !`command` and ```! blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`". The :570 table further binds a forked skill's system prompt to the agent type and its task to the SKILL.md content.
  > Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation.
- **У нас.** All four keys are parsed by nothing. `SkillMetadataSchema` is `.passthrough()` and declares none of them (packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:268-286); `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` (validation.ts:212-221) omits them; `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (validation.ts:246-251) lists all four with reasons, and its only consumer is validation.ts:352-359, which emits an author-facing WARNING ("'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored"). Pinned by packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.test.ts:60-72. The runtime read of a SKILL.md is `materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:831-902): it takes `allowed-tools`/`tools` (:869), `model` (:870), `agent` (:871), `effort` (:850) and `disallowed-tools` (:877-881) into `restrictions` and reads no `context`, `background`, `hooks` or `shell`. `RuntimeSkillHandle` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:69-109) carries no fork field either. The invocation body then goes INLINE into the live conversation: `formatPinnedSkillInstructions` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2395-2399) joins `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation` output (runtime-skill-content.ts:1075-1078) and it is injected on the model path at base-agent.ts:2676-2679 ("You invoked the skill above. The neighbouring `agent` field IS honoured but with different meaning: `applySkillInvocationGrant` (base-agent.ts:2540-2564) turns it into a per-turn agent CEILING via `setSkillInvocationAgentCeiling` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prerequisite-manager.ts:212-214) and throws `Invoked skill agent unavailable` at :2558 — never a spawn target. The repo's own `fork` is the opposite construct: `FORK_AGENT_NAME`/`FORK_AGENT_DEFINITION` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:208-232) is described as "a subagent that inherits the full message history, system prompt, tools and model of this session" (:221), reached by `/subtask` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6295-6310 `requestSubtaskFork`) and admitted at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10833-10839; no skill frontmatter routes into it. For `shell`, the in-file reason ("inline shell blocks always run under bash") overstates what exists: `expandRuntimeSkillBody` (runtime-skill-content.ts:629-699) performs variable and `$ARGUMENTS` substitution only, with no `` !`command` `` pass at all, and the plugin importer treats that syntax as an unsupported deferral in Claude prompt commands (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657, :741-749); `grep -a disableSkillShellExecution` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing. For `hooks`, frontmatter hook declarations in plugin-supplied skills and agents are refused out loud with a deferral (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:410-436 `reportFrontmatterHookDeclarations`), but no per-skill hook scope exists. Plugin-imported skills project only description, `disableModelInvocation`, `userInvocable`, `allowedTools` and `paths` (format-adapters.ts:517-552 `applyPluginSkillFrontmatter`), so a plugin skill's `context: fork` is dropped silently at import with no deferred row.
- **Пользователь.** Observable, and worst for installed plugins. A user runs a skill written for Claude Code with `context: fork` — say a research or PR-summary skill whose whole point is a throwaway context — and instead of a background subagent returning a summary, the entire SKILL.md is spliced into the live conversation and executed there: full history visible to the task (the opposite of what the skill's prompt assumes), the main context window consumed by the skill's own work, no separate background completion message, and no way to keep working while it runs. Nothing at invocation time says so. The author-facing warning added by 55b711ce is reachable only through an explicit `skill_validate` call (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/skill-validate.ts:116-129) or the config-doctor aggregate (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:487); the write-time gate at packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:509-517 acts on `!validationResult.valid` only, so warnings are dropped when a SKILL.md is written through a tool. And a Claude PLUGIN whose skill sets `context: fork` imports as fully supported — `applyPluginSkillFrontmatter` (format-adapters.ts:517-552) never looks at the key, so unlike a frontmatter `hooks` block there is no deferred row in Sources and no diagnostic anywhere. `background` and `shell` produce no separate symptom beyond this. One direction where we are safer, not worse: skills.md:559 warns that a backgrounded fork's edits escape `/rewind`; ours run inside the session and stay checkpointed.

#### f074 · `agent-sdk/slash-commands`

The delta is the whole mechanism, not a key name or a value: no code path anywhere resets conversation context in response to `/clear`. Three specific gaps, in the order they must be closed. (a) CLASSIFICATION — `parseSessionCommand` (session-command.ts:45) does not claim `clear`, so `BaseAgent.chat` (:2758) prefixes turn context and the bare command stops existing before any backend sees it. (b) EXECUTION — no backend has a `clear` arm: PiAgent's `runSessionCommand` (pi-agent.ts:6355) handles `compact`/`subtask` only, and ClaudeAgent's `SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS` (claude-agent.ts:1665) is `['compact']`. (c) EFFECT — the two functions that would do the work (`clearSessionMessages`, storage.ts:457; `clearHistory`, base-agent.ts:1605 and the three overrides) have zero production callers. Note the fix is NOT "add 'clear' to SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS": per slash-commands.md:214 an SDK-dispatched `/clear` inside our per-turn one-shot `query()` is not what produces empty context — dropping the `resume:` anchor (`this.sessionId = null`, already implemented in ClaudeAgent.clearHistory at :2745) is. Also note ClaudeAgent.clearHistory (:2745-2752) never calls `super.clearHistory()`, so even the existing dead implementation would skip the base resets at base-agent.ts:1606-1618.

- **Документация связывает.** slash-commands.md:212 binds `/clear` as a dispatchable session command: "The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history. The previous conversation remains on disk and can be returned to by passing its session ID to the [`resume` option]". The page's intro (:9) and the `system/init` example (:26) list `clear` beside `compact` in `slash_commands`. Two qualifiers scope the fix rather than excuse it: :214 says a one-shot `query()` already starts empty so `/clear` there has no practical effect (ours are NOT empty — every turn passes `resume`), and :217 gates it on Claude Code v2.1.117+ (bundled SDK is @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183, binary 2.1.183).
  > The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history.
- **У нас.** Nothing in the product implements a context reset for `/clear`; it is submitted to the model as prose on every backend. (1) The one classifier that decides "this text is an instruction to the SESSION" claims only `/compact` and `/subtask`: `parseSessionCommand`, packages/shared/src/slash-commands/session-command.ts:45 (COMPACT_PATTERN :38, subtask :54). (2) The single send seam therefore composes turn context onto the front of `/clear`: `BaseAgent.chat`, packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2758 returns early only when `parseSessionCommand(message)` is truthy; otherwise it builds `messageParts = [capabilityContext, branchSeedContext, transferredSessionContext, continuationRestore, pinnedSkills, runtimeSkillContext, cleanMessage]` (base-agent.ts:2816-2817), so the slash is no longer leading. (3) ClaudeAgent's own allowlist excludes it: `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;` packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1665, matched at :1670-1674 — and by then the message is already context-prefixed, so the `^\/([a-z]+)` match cannot fire anyway. The message goes to `buildTextPrompt` (claude-agent.ts:2429-2468), which pushes `contextParts` first and the user text last, into `query({ prompt, options })` at claude-agent.ts:1702 with `resume: this.sessionId` still set (claude-agent.ts:1607-1610). (4) PiAgent has the same hole: `chatImpl` classifies with the same function (pi-agent.ts:6477) and `runSessionCommand` (pi-agent.ts:6355) has arms for `compact` and `subtask` only. (5) The implementation functions exist and are dead: `clearSessionMessages` (packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:457, doc-comment :454 "Used for /clear command") has no production caller — `grep -rna` finds only its re-export at packages/shared/src/sessions/index.ts:67; `clearHistory` is implemented on all four backends (base-agent.ts:1605, claude-agent.ts:2745, pi-agent.ts:7151, nestor-cloud-agent.ts:194) and every non-test caller is absent (only pinned-capability-delivery.test.ts:152, pi-agent-lifecycle-hooks.test.ts:186, session-start-compact.test.ts:236/:257). (6) The command is nevertheless shipped and user-reachable: menu entry `clearCommand` — id `clear`, label "Clear", description "Clear the current conversation" — apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:162-167; exposed to every backend by `slash: { commandIds: 'all' }`, packages/shared/src/agent/backend/composer-capabilities.ts:103; `dispatchSlashCommandAction` falls past every UI-handler branch to `MESSAGE_COMMANDS.clear = '/clear'` (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/slash-command-actions.ts:55-57, :138-145) and calls `submitCommand`, wired to `onSubmit(command, undefined)` at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:1034 — an ordinary message. Asserted as intended today by apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/__tests__/slash-command-actions.test.ts:112-123.

Selecting it submits the literal text `/clear` as an ordinary turn (slash-command-actions.ts:57 → FreeFormInput.tsx:1034): the user sees their own "/clear" message in the transcript, the model replies to it as prose, a full context-wrapped turn is billed, and nothing is cleared — the next turn still resumes the same SDK/Pi session with the entire history (claude-agent.ts:1607-1610). (en.json:601) — so the product's own documented recovery is a no-op and the session stays stuck over the window; the only real exit is starting a new session. Also silently latent: no SessionStart `clear` source or SessionEnd `clear` reason ever fires, so a user automation matching `clear` never runs.

The entire mechanism is absent, not misnamed and not narrowed: no `/btw` command id, no parser, no non-persisting answer channel, no ephemeral overlay, no earlier-answers list, no fork-from-overlay. Two of the doc's four ingredients do have substrate — a tool-less single-response model call (`queryLlm`) and an in-memory transcript to feed it (`managed.messages`) — but they are not connected, and the one path that connects a user's text to a model today is the path that writes history. So the missing piece is specifically a send route that reads the transcript, answers once with no tools, and never touches `managed.messages`/`persistSession`, plus a renderer overlay to hold the answer. Two sub-behaviours are additionally unbuildable on today's primitives without extra work: prompt-cache reuse of the parent conversation (our `queryLlm` runs an ephemeral Pi session with no history) and the `f` fork into a new session inheriting the parent transcript plus the Q/A as real turns.

A user who follows Claude's docs and types `/btw what was the name of that config file again?` into the Nessy composer gets no `btw` entry in the `/` menu (nothing matches the filter at slash-command-menu.tsx:271), and on Enter the literal text is sent to the model as a normal prompt: it becomes a permanent user turn in the transcript, is persisted, mirrored and exported, consumes main-context tokens, and interrupts or queues behind the running turn — the four things the command exists to avoid. `/recap` behaves the same way, and additionally the model is being asked to recap while having no idea it was a command. There is also no automatic recap when the user returns to an idle session. Separately observable: typing `:heart:` inserts the literal characters (no emoji), and after `! npm test` the command output lands in the transcript but Claude does not respond to it, so the user must send a second prompt to get the failure explained — Claude Code has responded automatically since v2.1.186. Not observable: `editorMode`/`vimInsertModeRemaps`, which would need a composer-side editor mode to have any surface at all.

#### f210 · `troubleshooting`

The whole mechanism is missing, not a renamed field: no `/heapdump` command on any surface (desktop slash menu, CLI, agent-callable allowlist), no V8 snapshot writer, no `-diagnostics.json` breakdown, and no `~/Desktop`/home output path. Two secondary deltas matter for the fix. (a) Shape: the only memory data we produce is `ServerStatus.memory = { heapUsed, heapTotal, rss }` (packages/core/src/types/server.ts:25-29) — three counters delivered over RPC to a caller that never displays them, where the doc requires four buckets (resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, unaccounted native memory) persisted to a file; `arrayBuffers`/`external` are not even sampled, so the JS-versus-native discrimination the doc says the breakdown exists for is impossible today. (b) Process topology: Claude Code dumps the single CLI process, while here the memory can grow in the Electron main (which hosts SessionManager and the Pi client in-process) or in the Pi agent subprocess, so a faithful implementation has to name which process each artifact came from — a decision the page does not make for us.

- **Документация связывает.** `troubleshooting.md` line 39 binds the memory-recovery path to a user-runnable command: "If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`. On Linux without a Desktop folder, the files are written to your home directory." Line 41 fixes the two artifacts and the breakdown's contents: "The breakdown shows resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, and unaccounted native memory, which helps identify whether the growth is in JavaScript objects or in native code. To inspect retainers, open the `.heapsnapshot` file in Chrome DevTools under Memory -> Load; the breakdown is the file ending in `-diagnostics.json`." Line 44 (Warning) fixes the privacy contract: "The `.heapsnapshot` file contains every string in the process. Don't attach it to a public issue or share it. Attach only the `-diagnostics.json` file when reporting a memory issue ... That file contains memory statistics and no conversation content or credentials." So: one command, two files in `~/Desktop` (home fallback), a `.heapsnapshot` V8 snapshot, and a `-diagnostics.json` carrying exactly the four counters and nothing else. Steps 1-4 of the same section are already satisfied here (`/compact` exists at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/slash-command-actions.ts:56, `--safe-mode` at apps/cli/src/index.ts:129) — only the heapdump step is unbuilt.
  > If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`.
- **У нас.** Nothing writes a heap snapshot anywhere in the fork, and no surface offers to. (1) Absence, NUL-safe: `grep -rai 'heapdump|heap_dump|writeHeapSnapshot|heapsnapshot' packages apps scripts docs-site --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.json' --include='*.md'` returns zero hits; no production file imports `node:v8` or `node:inspector` (`grep -rai "from 'v8'|from 'node:v8'|require('v8')|node:inspector" packages apps scripts` -> zero). (2) The desktop slash-command surface has no memory command: the id union at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:17 is `PermissionMode | CustomSlashCommandId | 'agents' | 'automations' | 'compact' | 'context' | 'create-skill' | 'create-plugin' | 'export' | 'init' | 'memory' | 'model' | 'clear' | 'help' | 'subtask' | 'usage'` (`'memory'` there is session MEMORY.md — slash-command-menu.tsx:176-180, dispatched to `openMemory` at slash-command-actions.ts:114-117 — not process memory), `featureCommands` at :225-240 lists those fourteen, and the dispatcher at slash-command-actions.ts:76-148 has no diagnostic branch. (3) The agent-callable slash allowlist is `new Set(['compact', 'help'])` — packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10. (4) The CLI has no such command: the help text at apps/cli/src/index.ts:2043-2075 lists `run`, `doctor`, `plugin …`, `ping`, `health`, `versions`, `workspaces`, `sessions`, `connections`, `sources`, `session …`; `health` is `credentials:healthCheck` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:305-309) and `doctor` is scoped read-only to configuration by construction (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:1-24 docblock) and reports nothing about memory. (5) The nearest existing memory read is three counters over RPC, not a dump: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 does `const mem = process.memoryUsage()` and returns `memory: { heapUsed, heapTotal, rss }` on `server:getStatus`, typed at packages/core/src/types/server.ts:25-29; :123-131 adds a pass/fail check at 1.5 GB heap in `getHealthCheck`. `arrayBuffers` and `external` are read nowhere in the repo (`grep -rn -a 'arrayBuffers|mem.external' packages apps` -> zero), so even the four documented buckets have no partial coverage. (6) No wire channel exists to ask for one: the `server` namespace in packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:11-19 holds eight channels (`getWorkspaces`, `createWorkspace`, `getStatus`, `getHealth`, `getActiveSessions`, `shuttingDown`, `statusChanged`, `homeDir`). (7) The one debug affordance that could host it is dev-only: apps/electron/src/main/menu.ts:193 gates the Debug submenu on `!app.isPackaged`, and its three items are update-check, install-update and a reset-to-defaults message box (:196-227), so a packaged build has no diagnostic menu at all.
- **Пользователь.** Today a user whose Nessy Desktop climbs into the gigabytes has no way to produce a shareable artifact. The `/` menu shows fourteen feature commands and none concerns process memory (`/memory` opens session MEMORY.md); `nessy-general-agent --help` lists no memory command and `doctor` reports configuration only; the Debug menu that could host one is compiled out of packaged builds (apps/electron/src/main/menu.ts:193 `!app.isPackaged`). The three counters we do compute (`server:getStatus`) are never rendered — the Settings server page reads the unrelated `settings:getServerStatus` — so even the numbers are invisible. Practical consequence: a memory report from a real user can only say 'it got slow', and nobody can tell JS-heap growth from native growth, or tell the Electron main apart from the Pi subprocess. Nothing breaks until someone tries to diagnose a leak; the moment they do, the documented recovery step simply does not exist.

#### f094 · `workflows`

One missing rule, not a wrong value: workflow-spawned children take the ordinary subagent inheritance path, so their effective mode is the parent's mode, whereas the page binds them to a floor of `acceptEdits`. Only the `default` parent case actually diverges on the write axis — `auto` and `bypassPermissions` already rank above `acceptEdits`, so a floor is a no-op there. Nothing in the child spawn is even labelled as belonging to a workflow at the permission seam: `PiChildRestrictionsV1` has no workflow marker, and the only workflow signal that already reaches the host is the record's `ownerTaskId`, which a workflow run mints as `owner-workflow-<runId>` (workflow-tool.ts:460-461) versus `owner-subagent-<runId>` for a plain fan-out (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:489-490) — a distinction SessionManager already parses at :2072-2074 (`isGeneratedPiOrchestrationOwnerTaskId`). Secondary, scoping-only delta: the page says "regardless of your session's mode", which would also raise a `plan`/`explore`/`dontAsk` session's workflow children into write-capable territory; that is a genuine widening of our narrow-only clamp invariant (A1) and is the one point where the fix should deviate deliberately rather than copy the sentence.

- **Документация связывает.** workflows.md:181 (§ Approve the plan before it runs): "Your permission mode controls only the launch prompt above. The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your tool allowlist, regardless of your session's mode. File edits are auto-approved." The floor is edits-only, not blanket: :183 keeps shell commands, web fetches and non-allowlisted MCP tools prompting mid-run, and :185 scopes the whole paragraph away from `claude -p`/Agent SDK. So a workflow-spawned child must run at an effective permission mode of at least `acceptEdits` even when the launching session is in `default`.
  > The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode.

The spawn goes through the same `spawnChildSession` as an ordinary subagent (`options.spawn ?? spawnChildSession`, workflow-tool.ts:466), whose child restrictions forward a mode only when the AGENT DEFINITION carries one: `...(args.agentDef.permissionMode === undefined ? {} : { permissionMode: args.agentDef.permissionMode })` (spawner.ts:575); omission means "inherit the parent's mode verbatim" (spawner.ts:328-330; packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:44-50). Host-side the inheritance is narrow-only: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10406-10417 sets `childPermissionMode = record.restrictions.permissionMode ? clampPermissionModeToParent(requested, parentPermissionMode) : parentPermissionMode` and hands it to `createSession` at :10434, with the same narrow-only rule for nested ceilings at :10910-10934. Because `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` ranks acceptEdits(4) above default(3) (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:63) and `clampPermissionModeToParent` returns the stricter of the two (mode-types.ts:121-131), `clamp('acceptEdits','default')` yields `'default'` — the floor is unreachable from a default-mode session even if an agent def asked for it explicitly. The consequence is live: packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1660-1674 enables `autoAllowFileWrites` only when `effectivePermissionMode === 'acceptEdits'`, and :1931-1949 mints a `file_write` PromptInfo for every FILE_WRITE_TOOLS call when that flag is false; the child is `hidden: true` (SessionManager.ts:10442) but its prompt is deliberately routed to the nearest visible ancestor by `permissionSurfaceRouting` (SessionManager.ts:6467-6486), so the modal reaches the human. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/ packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing (only unrelated test fixtures elsewhere in the package). The OTHER half of the same doc paragraph IS built: launch consent (packages/shared/src/workflows/workflow-launch-consent.ts; gate context at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:708-743; `workflow_launch` prompt at pre-tool-use.ts:1534-1551) and tool-allowlist inheritance by the child session.
- **Пользователь.** Concrete and bad on the most common setup. In the Desktop app, from a session in the DEFAULT permission mode (the shipped default), launch a workflow — the `ultracode`/keyword route, the `workflow` tool, or a saved `/<name>` — and approve the launch card. From then on every single file edit by every spawned agent raises its own approval modal in the main session (`file_write`, pre-tool-use.ts:1944-1949, routed out of the hidden child by permissionSurfaceRouting), each agent blocking until it is answered, for a run the page presents as an unattended background fan-out in the Background tasks pane. A ten-agent workflow that touches three files each is thirty modals; unanswered children sit until the spawn deadline (spawner.ts:607, default 30 min) and the run then reports errors. The user's only workaround today is to switch the session to acceptEdits or auto BEFORE launching — which the doc explicitly says should not be necessary. Latent ("none observable") for sessions already in acceptEdits, auto or bypassPermissions, and for `claude -p`-equivalent headless runs which the page exempts anyway.

Three constraints the comment must record: (1) forks are excluded — a fork inherits the parent verbatim and the start handler already rejects a fork carrying a permissionMode (:10827); (2) the floor is gated on `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (mode-types.ts:98-100) so `plan`/`explore`/`dontAsk` parents keep their mode — a deliberate deviation from "regardless of your session's mode", because raising a no-write mode into a write-capable one is an escalation the clamp exists to prevent; (3) nothing else needs changing for nested agents — the raised mode becomes the child SESSION's `permissionMode` at :10434, so a grandchild's own depth-1 clamp reads the raised value and inherits it. The cleanup step is entirely absent; nothing about what we do run is wrong. The key name, the value and the enabling mechanism are git's own and correct — the delta is a missing post-removal `git config --local --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`, plus the two pieces of state that gate it per the doc's carve-out: an "we added it" ownership marker taken BEFORE the first sparse-set, and a "no worktrees left" count taken AFTER the remove. Because the ownership probe has to happen before the entry exists, this cannot be retrofitted as a removal-only change. One Nessy-specific wrinkle: leases are per session under one shared per-repo namespace root (`<parent-of-repo>/.nessy-worktrees/<repo>/<leaseId>`, SessionManager.ts:10105-10110), so "last worktree" must be computed from git (`git worktree list --porcelain`), not from one `WorktreeLeaseService` instance's lease list.

#### f201 · `scheduled-tasks`

The whole self-paced half of the page is absent, not mis-keyed. There is no `ScheduleWakeup` tool (no schema, no registry entry, no handler, no port method), no dynamic `/loop` iteration for it to re-arm or stop, no ~20-minute fallback wakeup, and no representation of a wakeup that is a delay rather than a cron expression — `SessionCronRecord` can only express a cron string, so even a correctly-named tool would have nothing to write. Two sub-deltas are narrower and independently real: (1) `cronJitterOffsetMs` would apply jitter to a dynamic loop, contradicting scheduled-tasks.md:74, because `SessionCronRecord` has no no-jitter field; (2) `session_crons` in Stop hook input is already correct by construction — anything stored as a record projects — so tools-reference.md:46's Stop-hook clause needs no work once the wakeup IS a record. The fixed-interval half of the page (5-field dialect, 8-char ids, 50 cap, seven-day expiry, ID-derived jitter, once-a-second tick, symlink refusal, `NESSY_DISABLE_CRON`/`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON`) is at parity and is not part of this divergence.

- **Документация связывает.** scheduled-tasks.md:130 binds a self-paced `/loop` to a model-callable `ScheduleWakeup` tool: "Claude calls the [`ScheduleWakeup` tool](/docs/en/tools-reference) with `stop: true`, which cancels the pending wakeup immediately", and "If an iteration ends without either rescheduling or stopping, Claude Code schedules one fallback wakeup about 20 minutes later and ends the loop when that iteration doesn't reschedule either." tools-reference.md:46 fixes the rest of the contract: ScheduleWakeup "Reschedules the next iteration of a [self-paced `/loop`] … Claude calls this at the end of each iteration to pick when the next one runs, between one minute and one hour out; you don't call it directly", `stop` is a named field, and "The pending wakeup appears in `session_crons` in [Stop hook input]". scheduled-tasks.md:74 adds that a dynamically scheduled loop "appears in your [scheduled task list] like any other task" and is subject to the seven-day expiry, but "The [jitter rules](#jitter) don't apply to it". The whole mechanism is missing — this is not a wrong key name or a wrong default. Three separate pieces are absent: (1) any per-session count of `web_search` calls; (2) the 200 default and its env lever (our spelling would be `NESSY_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION`, per this repo's documented rename convention at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:9-12); (3) the documented over-cap RESULT — a non-error notice telling the model to continue with what it has. Note the shape of (3): our failure path already returns `details: { isError: true }` (create-search-tool.ts:97, :109), and the cap must NOT use it, because the page explicitly contrasts the notice with "an error that would invite a retry". One further scope gap beyond the mechanism itself: because subagents are separate sessions/subprocesses, a counter that is merely per-process satisfies the default and the knob but not `tools-reference.md:432`'s "counted across the main conversation and every subagent it spawns" — a parallel research fan-out would get one full budget per child.

- **Документация связывает.** `whats-new/2026-w29.md:63` binds us to a session-wide WebSearch budget: "Session-wide caps stop runaway loops: WebSearch calls and subagent spawns each default to 200, tunable with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`". Two other snapshot pages give the semantics of the WebSearch half exactly. `env-vars.md:283`: "Cap on the total number of WebSearch calls one session can make (default: 200). When Claude reaches the cap, further WebSearch calls return a notice telling it to continue with the information it already gathered. Accepts a positive whole number with no upper bound. Anything else is ignored and the default applies, so the cap can be raised but not turned off." `tools-reference.md:432`: "A session can make at most 200 WebSearch calls, counted across the main conversation and every subagent it spawns, so searches made by parallel research fan-outs count against the same limit… When Claude reaches the limit, further calls return a notice telling Claude to continue with the information it already gathered, rather than an error that would invite a retry. You don't see the notice." So: one counter per session TREE (parent + every subagent), default 200, raisable-not-disablable via one env knob, and the over-cap result is a non-error notice, invisible to the user.

Two concrete consequences. On an OpenAI-API-key, ChatGPT-subscription or Google-key connection every single call is a billed upstream request (packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/resolve-provider.ts:58-86, providers/chatgpt.ts:100-110), so the same loop spends real quota or money with nothing to stop it. #### f102 · `memory`

The whole mechanism is absent: no writer inspects the first line for `---`, and no key named `modified` is ever emitted, so a memory file that DOES begin with frontmatter is appended to and left with a stale (or missing) timestamp forever. This is not a wrong key name for a right value: Nessy's nearest artefact, `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->`, differs on all four axes the doc fixes -- location (trailing HTML comment on the bullet, not a frontmatter key), granularity (one date per entry, not one timestamp per file), precision (calendar day, not ISO-8601 instant) and audience (stripped at load, so the model never sees it, versus a value the doc puts in front of both user and model). Renaming it would satisfy nothing. Conversely the doc's negative half is already satisfied by accident, not by design: because both writers seed a new file as `# Memory\n\n- ...`, Nessy never adds frontmatter to a file that has none -- so the observable gap is confined to files whose frontmatter a human hand-authored. One second-order divergence rides along and constrains the fix: Claude Code strips frontmatter before loading the index (`memory.md:388`, min-version 2.1.211), while `readMemoryFile` (`memory-store.ts:29-33`) reads the raw first 200 lines, so in this fork a frontmatter block -- and any `modified:` line we add -- becomes prompt content inside the `<memory>` block rather than metadata.

Read whole, the line adds the scope and the ceiling: "Any file that has frontmatter gets the field the next time Claude writes it, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none. The entire cap is absent — not a wrong constant, not a wrong key name, and not enforcement one layer up. All three of the page's obligations are missing together: no byte accounting (so no cap), therefore no clear error and no non-zero exit on breach. Two shape details the fix must get right, because getting either wrong would satisfy the letter and miss the point. (1) The cap must be measured on RAW BYTES read from the pipe (`value.byteLength`), not on the decoded string's `.length` — a UTF-8 multibyte payload would otherwise pass a character-count check well past 10MB. (2) It must fail FAST, cancelling the reader the moment the running total crosses the ceiling, not after the loop drains: the current code holds every chunk in `chunks` and then joins, so peak memory is roughly twice the input, and a post-hoc length check would still let a multi-gigabyte pipe exhaust memory before the error could be printed — which is the failure the cap exists to prevent. Separately, the error must reach the user as a clear message on BOTH paths: a throw from `cmdSend` is already caught by main()'s handler (apps/cli/src/index.ts:2242-2245 → `err(msg)` + `process.exit(1)`), but `run` is dispatched at :2132, BEFORE that `try` opens at :2184, so a throw out of `cmdRun` escapes main() entirely as an unhandled rejection instead of the documented clear error.

The whole mechanism is absent — this is not a key-name or value mismatch that a rename would fix. Four separable pieces are missing: (1) `policyHelper` is not a recognised managed key, so the admin-authored value is stripped rather than read; (2) nothing spawns the executable at `path` with `timeoutMs`, so no `managedSettings` envelope is ever parsed; (3) the managed tier has no helper seam, so even a parsed helper output could not become the single winning source ahead of `delivered` and `file`; (4) there is no `refreshIntervalMs` re-run timer and no non-zero-exit startup refusal for it. The precedence RULE we do implement is correct for the two sources we have — winner-takes-all, no merge (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:184-214`) — so the delta is the missing top rung of that ordering, not a wrong ordering. Scope note on the recorded justification: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-server-managed-delivery.md:212-215` puts `policyHelper` out of scope as "OS-policy sources only", which correctly excludes it from the server-DELIVERED channel (settings.md:633 agrees it is ignored there) but says nothing about the system-FILE scope, which the same sentence names as valid and which this fork ships. The audit row is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:193` (R25b, "Record as C" = documented, not implemented) — an open item, not a closed owner decision.

#### f184 · `keybindings`

This is an absent mechanism, not a wrong key name. Four separable deltas: (1) NO CONFIG FILE OR LOADER — nothing reads a `keybindings.json`, so the declared `userOverrides` map (registry.tsx:31) is permanently empty and no user can rebind anything by any route; the doc's `$schema`/`$docs`/`bindings` object, its `context` blocks, and the live-reload requirement (:15) have no counterpart. (2) VOCABULARY SPELLING — the concept of a namespaced action id exists but uses a dot (`app.newChat`) where the page uses a colon (`app:newChat`, :71); the file-level `context` names (:45-65, nineteen of them) have no counterpart at all — our nearest analogue is the six-key `when`-clause context (keybinding-context.ts:18-31), and even the four-value `ActionScope` is dead metadata. (3) KEYSTROKE GRAMMAR — our parser accepts `mod|shift|alt` only (registry.tsx:141-143) against the page's `ctrl|control`, `shift`, `alt|opt|option|meta`, `cmd|command|super|win` (:354-357); it has no chord sequencing (:378-382) and no prefix reservation (:410); and its blanket `toLowerCase()` (:139) cannot express the `K` = `shift+k` / `ctrl+K` = `ctrl+k` asymmetry (:372-374). (4) NO DISCOVERY OR VALIDATION — no `/keybindings` command entry (slash-command-menu.tsx:17) and none of the five documented warning classes (:470-480). What is already right and must not be re-derived: `null` as the unbound sentinel, the override-before-default precedence in `getHotkey` (registry.tsx:59-65), and a single capture-phase dispatcher the overrides feed into (:80-108).

Run `/keybindings` to create or open your configuration file at `~/.claude/keybindings.json`." The file's shape is fixed by :13-38 — an object with optional `$schema` and `$docs` plus a `bindings` array whose blocks each carry a `context` string and a `bindings` map of keystroke -> action; actions are spelled `namespace:action` (:71, e.g. `chat:externalEditor`); a keystroke mapped to `null` unbinds the default (:395); chords are space-separated keystroke sequences (:378-382) and a chord prefix stays reserved until every chord sharing it is unbound (:410); modifiers are `ctrl`/`control`, `shift`, `alt`/`opt`/`option`/`meta`, `cmd`/`command`/`super`/`win` joined with `+` (:354-357), a standalone uppercase letter implies Shift while an uppercase letter with a modifier does not (:372-374); the file reloads live — "Changes to the keybindings file are automatically detected and applied without restarting Claude Code" (:15); and the loader must warn on parse errors, invalid context names, reserved-shortcut conflicts, multiplexer conflicts and duplicate bindings in the same context, writing each warning to the debug log (:470-480).

The whole mechanism is an in-memory stub: `apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/registry.tsx:23` is the comment `// User hotkey overrides (future: load from config)`, :24 declares `userOverrides: Map<ActionId, string | null>` on the context type, :31 creates it as `useRef(new Map())`, and :61-62 / :116 are its only reads — `grep -rna userOverrides` over all .ts/.tsx returns exactly those five hits, so it is never written and `getHotkey` (:59-65) always falls through to `actions[actionId].defaultHotkey`. - **Пользователь.** A user cannot rebind any keyboard shortcut in Nessy Desktop, and there is no surface that tells them so. Settings -> Shortcuts (ShortcutsPage.tsx) and the Cmd+/ Keyboard Shortcuts dialog both render the 27 defaults as static `<kbd>` chips with no edit affordance and no link to a config file; typing `/keybindings` in the composer matches no command. Concretely: `mod+q` is hardwired to app.quit, `escape` to chat.stopProcessing, `mod+a` to navigator.selectAll — a user whose muscle memory or accessibility setup needs a different chord has no route, and a user arriving from Claude Code who drops a `~/.claude/keybindings.json`-shaped file anywhere sees it silently ignored (no warning, no debug line). The whole missed-run mechanism is absent, not narrowed: no persisted per-task last-occurrence cursor, no start-time sweep, no wake trigger, no seven-day window, no discard-older rule, no catch-up notification. Two specifics that shape the fix. (a) It is not enough to make the sweep re-emit `SchedulerTick`: `matchesBasePredicate` (utils.ts:289) evaluates the cron against the CURRENT minute, so a replayed tick matches nothing — the sweep needs its own matcher-selection path, not a synthetic tick. (b) The nearest existing timestamp, automation history `ts` (webhook-utils.ts:65), is the RUN time, not the scheduled occurrence, and is capped at 20 entries per matcher; using it as the cursor would double-fire or silently skip. The cursor must be the OCCURRENCE time and must live in its own durable file. The sibling session-scoped Cron tier already has the correct discipline and the correct reason written down (packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts:144-165: stamp at delivery, not enqueue; packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts:121-131), but it implements the opposite contract (scheduled-tasks.md:215 forbids per-interval catch-up), is per-session and non-durable, and explicitly is not `SchedulerService` (session-cron-service.ts:9-16) — so it supplies a pattern to copy, not the behaviour.

- **Документация связывает.** desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:74 (§ Missed runs) binds the durable scheduler to a start/wake sweep: "When the app starts or your computer wakes, Desktop checks whether each task missed any runs in the last seven days. If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older. A daily task that missed six days runs once on wake. Desktop shows a notification when a catch-up run starts." So: a per-task cursor of the last fired occurrence, a seven-day window, exactly ONE fire per task at the most recent missed occurrence, everything older discarded, and a notification on that fire. :70 ("If your computer sleeps through a scheduled time, the run is skipped") governs the in-session minute tick, not the wake sweep.
  > If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older.

- **Пользователь.** Concrete and silent. A user creates a scheduled automation in the Automations UI — say cron `0 9 * * *` with a prompt action — and closes the laptop overnight. Not a key-name or value mismatch — the parsed decision is already correct and correctly spelled. The delta is one missing awaited round trip: the `PreCompact` emission on Pi is fire-and-forget (`Promise<void> | void`, lifecycle-bridge.ts:28), so a `block` that the contract layer produced has no path back to the `session_before_compact` handler's return value, and Pi's `{ cancel: true }` is therefore never returned. Exit code 2 is inert for the same reason (it becomes the same discarded `{ decision: 'block' }`). Scope: Pi only. The identical hook blocks correctly on the Claude backend (hooks-automation.ts:1673-1681), so the divergence is per-runtime, not global — and Pi is the default and the only backend enabled by default.

For a manual `/compact`, the stderr message is shown to the user. You can also block by returning JSON with `\"decision\": \"block\"`." hooks.md:2657 fixes what a blocked auto-compact does: a proactive compaction is skipped and "the conversation continues uncompacted"; a compaction triggered to recover from a context-limit error lets "the underlying error surface". hooks.md:2661 also binds the input to `trigger` and `custom_instructions`.

Nothing on Pi consumes the result. - **Пользователь.** Observable today on the default build. A user who adds a PreCompact automation with a blocking action (Automations surface / packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts), or installs a Claude plugin whose `PreCompact` hook exits 2, watches the hook run and the compaction happen anyway: typing `/compact` still returns "Compacted context to fit within limits …" (pi-agent.ts:6363) and the history is summarised away, and auto-compaction at the context threshold does the same. Nothing tells them the block was dropped — the reason is parsed, then discarded at pi-agent.ts:2340, and no `__HOOK_BLOCK__` line is even logged for this event. The concrete loss is the guard case the doc exists for: "do not compact while this plan is mid-execution" / "snapshot before compacting" cannot be enforced, and a hook author who tested against Claude Code sees the opposite behaviour here. It is not latent and not uniform: rebuild with `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1` and run the Claude backend and the same hook blocks correctly (hooks-automation.ts:1673-1681), so the same configuration behaves two ways depending on the backend.

No new transport, no new field, no schema change: the alias must collapse to the existing `'http'` value before the transport switch.

Every JSON reader of an MCP server entry must treat the `type` value `streamable-http` as exactly equal to `http` (same `url`, `headers`, `oauth`, `timeout`, `alwaysLoad` handling), not as an unknown transport.

#### f134 · `channels`

Two deltas, both in delivery semantics of a feature we do ship — not absence. (a) IDLE ARRIVAL IS NOT SUPPORTED. The doc's only precondition is that the session is open; ours is that a turn is in flight. And the cause is one layer deeper than the `canDeliver()` gate the finding cites: the subscription is created and destroyed with the turn, so an event arriving between turns has no listener to reach and is discarded inside `McpClientPool.dispatchChannelMessage` before any session-level gate runs. Fixing only `canDeliver` would change nothing. (b) NO GROUPING. Several events during a busy turn are each `redirect()`-ed into the running turn immediately, where the contract is one grouped delivery in arrival order on the NEXT turn. Note what is NOT wrong: the policy/gate layer (`ChannelPolicy`, `resolveManagedChannelPolicy`, fail-closed default) is correct and deliberate, and the grouped-delivery machinery already exists — this is a wiring gap between `pool.subscribeChannel` and `deliverMonitorEvent`, plus a lifetime change on the subscription. Adjacent and NOT part of this delta (it gates any live verification): our client reads `params.text` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361`) while the documented field is `params.content`, and we never emit the `<channel source=... >` wrapper or `meta` attributes.

- **Документация связывает.** channels.md:13 binds a channel to being "an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal", and states exactly one precondition for arrival — "Events only arrive while the session is open" — not that a turn is in flight. The sibling delivery contract at channels-reference.md:256 adds: "Events queue into the session and are processed in order. If several notifications arrive while Claude is busy, they're delivered together on the next turn and Claude handles them as a group." The documented notification is `notifications/claude/channel` with `params.content` (the event body) and `params.meta` (attributes on the emitted `<channel source=...>` tag) — channels-reference.md:229, :238.
  > A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal.
- **У нас.** We ship the channel push path, but it can only steer a turn that is already running, and it steers each event in individually. (1) The subscription itself is TURN-PINNED. `pool.subscribeChannel` has exactly one production call site, inside `armPiPluginPeripherals` — `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` (`managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })`). That method is called only from the send path, `SessionManager.ts:13127` in `getOrCreateAgentUnchecked`, and `disarmPluginPeripherals` (`SessionManager.ts:2381-2387`) removes the listener in `sendMessage`'s finally (`SessionManager.ts:15778`), in `withCapabilityRuntime`'s finally (`:5898`) and in `disposeManagedAgentRuntime` (`:9614`, `:9747`). So between turns there is no subscriber at all: the pool's `dispatchChannelMessage` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1106`) iterates `this.channelSubscribers.get(leaserId)`, finds an empty set, and the event dies in the pool with no error returned to the pushing server. The field's own comment says so — "Ephemeral claude/channel listener" (`SessionManager.ts:1272-1273`). (2) Even with a listener present, `canDeliver()` (`SessionManager.ts:2399-2405`) returns `undefined` unless BOTH `managed.isProcessing` and `agent.isProcessing?.()` hold, plus a capability-generation match (`:2403`). Not a wrong key name and not a missing value: the positional family is simply not implemented on the command path. `$ARGUMENTS` and the legacy Nessy `{{args}}` expand correctly; `$0`, `$1`, `$ARGUMENTS[N]` and `\$1` escaping do not, so those placeholders reach the model as literal text. The correct 0-based, quote-aware, single-pass implementation the page describes already exists 200 lines away in `runtime-skill-content.ts` but is module-private and reachable only from the skill materializer. Second-order: the plugin importer's detector for the same construct is `/\$[1-9]\b/`, which misses `$0` (the FIRST argument per skills.md:302) and `$ARGUMENTS[N]` entirely, and native plus workflow commands get no deferral notice at all.

#### f143 · `code-review`

The review ENGINE exists and is wired; the documented ENTRY POINT and four contract details do not. (1) No user-invocable command: `review` is model-invocable only, the exact inverse of the doc's `disable-model-invocation` (:339). (2) Wrong default scope: ours is uncommitted-only (review-tool.ts:83) where the doc's is "branch's commits ahead of its upstream plus any uncommitted changes" (:295) — an upstream-relative diff we never compute. (3) Narrower target grammar: `base` (merge-base) and `commit` only; no file path, no PR number, no `main...my-feature` ref range, and no `ultra`. (4) No `--fix` and no `--comment`; `--comment` has no underlying GitHub mechanism anywhere in the repo. (5) Foreground-only: `background: false` is hard-coded (review-tool.ts:316), so the doc's background-subagent default and its three named foreground fallbacks are all collapsed into the fallback. (6) Findings ride a different shape: our P0-P3 `title/body/priority/confidence` object rendered as text, not `ReportFindings`' `file/summary/failureScenario/category` (:312) — same information, incompatible keys, and no `category` slug. (7) Cleanup findings absent: the rubric flags introduced defects only, where :285 also binds "reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups". (8) No per-invocation effort argument (:324). Also a fork-internal contradiction: our docs-site documents `/review` as a built-in slash command and no such command exists.

- **Документация связывает.** code-review.md:285 binds a user-invocable `/code-review` command that "reviews a diff in your terminal" and "reports correctness bugs and reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups". Its contract, one layer down the same page: default scope is "your branch's commits ahead of its upstream plus any uncommitted changes" (:295); a target may be "a file path, a PR number, a branch name, or a ref range such as `main...my-feature`" (:295); flags are `--fix` ("applies the findings to your working tree after the review") and `--comment` ("posts the findings as inline PR comments") (:299-:300); an effort level may precede them and absent it "the review uses the session's current effort" (:324); without `ultra` "everything left is the review target, even when it starts with another command name" (:328); the review "runs as a background subagent with its own context window" and falls back to the foreground when re-run while in progress, in `-p`/SDK mode, or when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` is `1` (:304, :333-:337); "When the host application requests it, Claude reports the review's findings through the `ReportFindings` tool" with a `category` tag such as `correctness` (:312); and the command "is marked `disable-model-invocation`" so a scheduled task reads it as plain text (:339). `/code-review ultra` escalates to cloud ultrareview and, when ultrareview is unavailable, "runs a local review in your session instead" (:343, :346). `/simplify` is the pre-v2.1.147 name and from v2.1.154 is a separate cleanup-only review (:353). :10 states the local command is available on every plan, so this is not a subscription-gated surface.
  > The [`/code-review` command](/docs/en/commands) reviews a diff in your terminal without installing the GitHub App.
- **У нас.** There is no `/code-review` (and no `/review`) command. The built-in command set is the `SlashCommandId` union at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:17 — `agents automations compact context create-skill create-plugin export init memory model clear help subtask usage` plus permission modes — and its prompt-macro table at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/slash-command-actions.ts:55-74 maps only `compact`, `clear`, `help`, `init`, `create-skill`, `create-plugin`. packages/shared/src/slash-commands/session-command.ts:38-57 recognises only `/compact` and `/subtask` as session commands, so any other `/word` line is sent to the model as prose. Exactly two bundled skills ship (apps/electron/resources/skills/plugin-creator/SKILL.md, apps/electron/resources/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md), resolved from the single root `getBundledAssetsDir('skills')` at packages/shared/src/utils/paths.ts:218-228, and packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:41-49 makes the bundle the sole authority on bundled slugs — so no seeded `code-review` skill can appear either.
