- **Пользователь.** Concrete and doubly bad, because our own docs advertise the missing command. A user reads docs-site/content/core-concepts/interactions.md:41 ("**`/review`** runs a dedicated, adversarial code review of a diff"), types `/review` in the composer, and nothing command-like happens: `/review` is not in the `/` menu (slash-command-menu.tsx:17), it is not a session command (session-command.ts:38-57), so the literal string is sent to the model as prose. `/code-review` behaves the same. Whether a review actually runs is then up to the model deciding to call the `review` tool on its own. When it does, the user gets a review that is narrower than the page they may have read: it covers only uncommitted changes — a user who has committed their branch work and typed `/code-review` expecting the documented "commits ahead of upstream" scope gets "No changes to review" — it blocks the turn instead of running in the background, it never applies its own fixes, it cannot take a PR number or a `main...my-feature` range, it reports no reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups, and its findings arrive as a P0-P3 text block rather than a rendered findings list.

Three deltas, all on the leading-run parse; none on argument expansion, which is already correct for a single skill.

1. RUN LENGTH. We match one command; the doc requires a run of up to six when the first is a skill. This is not a wrong key name or a wrong value — the loop does not exist, and the singular `customSlashCommandId` type makes it unrepresentable end to end.

2. ARGUMENT DISTRIBUTION. The doc gives the SAME trailing text to every expanded skill. Our nearest native equivalent, `[skill:...]` mentions, PARTITIONS text between markers instead: `runtimeSkillArguments` (`packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:606-617`) is "Arguments following the last matching `[skill:...]` reference, up to the next skill mention", so on `[skill:a] [skill:b] do XYZ` skill-a gets `""` and skill-b gets `do XYZ`. That partition semantics is CORRECT for the model-emitted path (`extractModelSkillInvocations`, `base-agent.ts:2166-2188`, where the model writes a distinct task per marker) and must not be changed. The stacked-command fix therefore has to emit the shared text after EACH marker — `[skill:a] do XYZ\n[skill:b] do XYZ` — which the existing partition logic then reads back as `do XYZ` for both. No edit to `runtime-skill-content.ts` is needed, and that is the load-bearing detail: the naive composition `[skill:a] [skill:b] do XYZ` would silently give the first skill empty arguments.

3. CAP AND STOP RULE. Neither exists, because there is no run to bound. The stop condition reduces cleanly to `custom:skill:`-prefixed membership of the composer's own command list (non-user-invocable skills never enter it, `custom-commands.ts:443`); the doc's forked-subagent clause has no analogue today and would only become live if a subagent skill mode is ever added.

#### f165 · `env-vars`

Not a key-name-only mismatch — one of the three obligations is entirely absent and the other two are wrong in value and in unit. (1) DISK SPILL: absent. The doc requires the full output on disk and its path inside the truncated response; we write no file and the marker is a bare `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` (subagent-tool.ts:177). The parent's only recourse is `get_subagent_result(agent_id)`, which is not the documented mechanism and by default returns 16 KiB — less than it already had. (2) TUNABILITY: absent. `OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES` is a hardcoded constant; `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` (and any `NESSY_*` analogue) is unread, so the documented 160000 ceiling is unreachable. (3) UNIT: we count UTF-8 BYTES (32768) where the doc counts CHARACTERS (32000). ASCII output is near-parity (32768 vs 32000 chars, ours slightly larger); two-byte text — Cyrillic, which is this fork's primary locale — is cut at ~16 384 characters, roughly half the documented budget, and CJK/emoji worse. A separate consequence of the same fixed number: even if the cap became tunable, values above 64 KiB would do nothing, because the host's read-side `MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (child-session-service.ts:42) is what the inline path receives.

- **Документация связывает.** env-vars.md:425 binds the subagent-output cap to `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`: "Maximum number of characters in subagent output before truncation (default: 32000, maximum: 160000). When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response". Three obligations: the cap counts CHARACTERS, it is user-tunable via that env var between the default 32000 and a 160000 maximum, and a truncated response must name the on-disk file holding the full output.

#### f220 · `whats-new/2026-w20`

Exactly one half of a two-part rule is missing: case (and trim) folding is implemented, separator folding is not. No key name, value, schema or wire field is wrong — the shapes are right and the fix is a comparison change, not a rename. The gap is symmetric across both comparison arms (requested name and stored name/aliases run through the same `normalizeName`), so it bites in two directions: a hyphen/underscore/space variant of a correctly-named agent is rejected, and an agent whose declared name contains a space is stored with that space and is unreachable by its kebab spelling. Consequence, stated accurately (the original finding overstated it as "the same class as the Task->Agent rename that broke every turn"): the call is REJECTED with a retryable tool error that enumerates the available agents, so the model can recover on the next tool call — not a broken turn. The one place it degrades further is under an active invoked-skill agent ceiling, where prerequisite-manager.ts:461 rejects first with a message carrying no agent list.

(1) PRIMARY, absent mechanism: the "Marker line" bullet has no implementation at all — no `[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):` prefix is ever prepended, and no permission-setting pattern exists, so a child report that mentions `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` matches nothing and arrives at the parent completely unannotated. Two deltas, one value and one missing mechanism. (a) VALUE: the default layer count is 1 where the page says 3. The key name, the counting convention (layers below the main conversation) and the at-limit enforcement point are all already right — only the number is wrong, in four places that must move together (`spawner.ts:110`, `harness-manifest.ts:107`, `SessionManager.ts:4932`, and the two tests that pin them). (b) MECHANISM: there is no configurable limit at all. Claude exposes it as `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (env or `settings.json` `env` block), so `1` is the documented OPT-OUT and any positive integer is settable; we expose it only as `orchestrator.depth` on the internal execution manifest, which no production path writes, so neither a user nor an admin can change nesting depth by any means. Note what is NOT part of this delta: at-limit behaviour differs separately and knowingly — sub-agents.md:861 says Claude "withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork" while we always return the `Subagent depth limit exceeded (N)` error from the call site (`spawner.ts:513-519` records that choice, which matches only the documented FORK behaviour). Raising the default to 3 does not fix that, and does not depend on it.

#### f017 · `permissions`

Three separate deltas, only one of which is cosmetic.

(1) The KEY NAME is absent, not merely unenforced. An administrator writing the documented `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` gets it stripped as unknown (managed-policy.ts:727-733); there is no alias, no partial parse. So even the surface we do enforce is unreachable through the documented spelling.

(2) The `hooks` surface has the right BEHAVIOUR under the wrong KEY. `allowManagedHooksOnly` produces exactly the doc's hooks row (user/project hook tiers dropped, force-enabled plugin hooks kept). This is a key-name-only divergence for that quarter: mapping `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: ['hooks']` onto the existing `managedHookLock.enabled` is a one-line OR at SessionManager.ts:11284.

(3) The `skills` and `agents` surfaces have NO mechanism of any kind — no key, no filter, no predicate. This is the real gap. Nothing in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` constrains the ORIGIN of a skill or an agent; `allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins` narrow plugins only, and narrowing plugins does not touch a native record. `availableModels` restricts which model a skill may use, never where the skill came from — an identically-shaped key in the same file that is not this control.

One parse rule also diverges in advance: the page requires unknown surface names to be IGNORED, while our list parser `list()` (managed-policy.ts:783-797) throws on any entry that fails validation, so a naive reuse of `grant`/`restrict` would fail the whole key on a future surface name — the opposite of what the page specifies.

Finally, the `mcp` surface is genuinely narrower than the doc rather than absent: `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` can deny named/URL/command-identified servers from native records (storage-runtime.ts:704-713), but there is no "only plugin and managed servers" pole — `allowedMcpServers: []` blocks plugin servers too (storage-runtime.ts:732-733).

- **Пользователь.** Concrete and permission-widening today. A CI operator who writes the documented lockdown, `nessy-general-agent run "Fix the lint" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read`, gets a run whose prompt is the literal string `Fix the lint --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read` and whose session is created at `bypassPermissions` (index.ts:842) — the most permissive mode, the opposite of what was asked, with no warning on stdout or stderr and exit code 0. The model additionally sees the flag text as part of its instructions. #### f194 · `output-styles`

Set composition, not mechanism. The output-style mechanism is fully built — discovery, frontmatter, trust-gated roots, plugin namespacing, `keep-coding-instructions` subtraction, prompt composition on both backends — and two of the four documented built-in names are simply missing from `BUILTIN_OUTPUT_STYLE_DEFINITIONS`: `Proactive` (an autonomy posture; we have no style-level equivalent, and the only nearby thing is the `auto` permission mode, which the same doc line calls weaker AND which changes permission gating that the doc says Proactive must not) and `Learning` (no collaborative style, and no `TODO(human)` marker convention anywhere in the repo). `Default` and `Explanatory` share the documented names; `Concise` and `Reviewer` are Nessy-authored extras with no Claude counterpart, which is an addition, not a defect. Explanatory's missing "Insights" convention is a distinct, already-registered row (deviation-register :226) and is NOT part of this delta. The consequence is narrower than the finding as originally filed: a user-authored `.md` DOES resolve, because `discoverCustomOutputStyles` (:465-508) is name-agnostic and registers any `.md` under a scanned root as `custom:<slug>`, so dropping `Proactive.md` into `~/.nessy-agent/output-styles` yields a working selectable style. `NO_OUTPUT_STYLE` (:562, returned at :570) is reached only by a stored `outputStyleId` that matches no built-in, plugin or custom style.

- **Документация связывает.** output-styles.md:17 makes **Default** "the existing system prompt", and :19 binds the product to "three additional built-in output styles": **Proactive** (:21 — "Claude executes immediately, makes reasonable assumptions instead of pausing for routine decisions, and prefers action over planning", explicitly "stronger autonomous-execution guidance than auto mode" and one that "works without changing your permission mode, so you still see permission prompts before tools run"), **Explanatory** (:23 — educational "Insights" interleaved with the work) and **Learning** (:25 — collaborative learn-by-doing that shares "Insights" and "will add `TODO(human)` markers in your code for you to implement"). The set is named, so a user or a doc-following config that asks for `Proactive` or `Learning` must get that style.
  > **Proactive**: Claude executes immediately, makes reasonable assumptions instead of pausing for routine decisions, and prefers action over planning.
- **У нас.** Our built-in set is four entries — `default`/Default, `concise`/Concise, `explanatory`/Explanatory, `reviewer`/Reviewer — declared in `BUILTIN_OUTPUT_STYLE_DEFINITIONS` at packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts:83-128 (default :85-91, concise :92-103, explanatory :104-115, reviewer :116-127), all with `keepCodingInstructions: true`. That array is the whole built-in surface: :130 derives `BUILTIN_OUTPUT_STYLE_IDS` from it, which is the accept-set of `isValidOutputStyleId` (:150-174, builtin branch :156-158); :518-524 `listOutputStyles` prepends it to the picker; :526-531 `resolveOutputStyle` matches a built-in id before any custom or plugin lookup. Neither `proactive` nor `learning` exists anywhere: `grep -ran` over `packages/` and `apps/` (excluding node_modules and dist) finds no built-in with either id and no `TODO(human)` marker string at all — the single "proactive" hit is packages/codex-protocol/generated/MultiAgentMode.ts:11, an unrelated Codex `MultiAgentMode` enum in a sibling subsystem. No layer above supplies the missing styles: both backends compose OUR block and append it to the vendor preset rather than selecting a vendor built-in — claude-agent.ts:1244-1258 passes `getOutputStyleId()` into `getSystemPrompt` as `presetAppend`, and pi-agent.ts:6586-6609 does the same through `resolveChildOutputStyleId`; prompts/system.ts:438-452 resolves the composition and system.ts:745-746 renders `getSafetyAndEngineeringSections(...)` then `${outputStylePrompt}`. The selection itself is the app-global `config.json:outputStyleId` (config/storage.ts:57, getter :2508-2511, setter :2513-2529, validator validators.ts:149), exposed over RPC at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/settings.ts:132-159 (`GET_OUTPUT_STYLE`, `SET_OUTPUT_STYLE` gated by `isValidOutputStyleId`, `LIST_OUTPUT_STYLES` at :148-159) and rendered by apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/settings/AiSettingsPage.tsx:1007-1025, which labels built-ins from `t('outputStyles.<id>.label', style.label)` against the eight keys at packages/shared/src/i18n/locales/en.json:931-938 and ru.json:935-942. - **Пользователь.** Settings → AI → Output style offers exactly four entries: Default, Concise, Explanatory, Reviewer. Separator set only. The rule grammar itself is correct and complete — `*`, exact host, `.suffix`, `host:port`, IPv4, `[::1]`, `[::1]:port` all parse and match as documented (network-proxy-utils.ts:219-293, covered by network-proxy.test.ts:40-124). - **Документация связывает.** network-config.md:30-33 documents TWO accepted spellings of the same variable, side by side: `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format` / `export NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` and `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - comma-separated format` / `export NO_PROXY="localhost,192.168.1.1,example.com,.example.com"`. A `NO_PROXY` parser must therefore treat whitespace as an entry separator exactly as it treats a comma. The page's note `All environment variables shown on this page can also be configured in settings.json` extends the same contract to the settings-side field (our `NetworkProxySettings.noProxy`, packages/shared/src/config/types.ts:31).

#### f116 · `amazon-bedrock`

No key is misspelled and no value semantics are wrong — the delta is purely the membership of the routing-var lists. Two lists are short by the same three names (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH`): options.ts:260-262 and `CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS` at llm-connections.ts:931-935. A third list, `MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION` (managed-env.ts:93-170), classifies the same three as `'immediate'` by default omission when the doc makes two of them provider routing and one an auth switch — they should be `'routing'`/`'routing'`/`'credential'` to sit beside their Invoke-API siblings. Consequence of the delta, not part of it: the invariant the code states ("Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path") is satisfied for the Invoke API and defeated for Mantle, and the managed-settings consent surface withholds one half of a Bedrock configuration while applying the other silently. Same shape, wider: the bundled binary also honours `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` (24 hits), `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` (19), `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS` (21) with `ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL` (16), and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY` (5), none of which the strip lists carry either — that overlap belongs to f118, and the fix below should be shaped as one shared provider-routing allowlist so it absorbs them rather than adding three more hardcoded deletes.

- **Документация связывает.** amazon-bedrock.md § "Use the Mantle endpoint" (line 433 of the .md): "Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. It uses the same AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and `awsAuthRefresh` configuration described earlier on this page." Three env vars select it — `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` (enable, `1` or `true`), `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` (override the endpoint URL), `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` (skip client-side auth for a gateway) — tabled at :495-497, and :460 states that setting `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` together lets one session call both endpoints. So the set of env vars that redirect a Claude Code process to Bedrock is six, not three: any code enforcing "Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path" is bound to all of them.
  > Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API.
- **У нас.** The sanitization mechanism exists and covers exactly the three Invoke-API vars. `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` builds the Claude SDK subprocess env by spreading the whole ambient environment — `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245) — then deletes three keys under the comment "Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path" (options.ts:257-262): `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`. That env feeds every spawn via `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:276). The same three-key list is duplicated as `CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935), wrapped by `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:969-975), which `ClaudeAgent.postInit` calls against the real `process.env` at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:917 under "Claude subprocesses must never inherit Bedrock-routing toggles from a previous connection or parent process environment", and which is spread into `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` (llm-connections.ts:941-950) so `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:977-990) deletes rather than restores them (baseline forced to `undefined` at :959-967). `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` appear nowhere in packages/, apps/ or scripts/ source (`grep -arn` over the tree hits only the doc-sweep artifacts under docs/superpowers/specs/ and the vendored `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:332857`, which is bundled SDK code, not ours), so all three survive the spread into the subprocess. The binary that receives them does honour them: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` (SDK pinned 0.3.183 by the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` dependency entry of the root package.json, packages/shared/package.json and packages/core/package.json) contains `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` 21 times, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` 14 and `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` 14. A third, independent site has the same omission: the managed-settings classification table `MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:93-170) lists `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` as `'routing'` (:123-126) and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` as `'credential'` (:143), while `classifyManagedEnvVar` defaults every unlisted name to `'immediate'` (managed-env.ts:190-192) — so a server-cache managed `env` block carrying the three Mantle vars is applied at once by `resolveManagedEnv`/`applyManagedEnv` (managed-env.ts:255-259, 345-354) with no withhold-and-confirm gate, unlike its `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` sibling. Nothing upstream compensates: our own Bedrock support runs through Pi's separate AWS path (`PiAgent.buildAwsEnv`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2038-2061, sets only `AWS_*`), and packages/shared/AGENTS.md:37 documents the sanitization as the active invariant, naming the same three vars.
- **Пользователь.** None observable for a default install — the vars have to be exported by the host shell (or arrive in a managed settings-cache `env` block) before anything changes. What makes it surface: a user on an AWS-integrated machine who has run the Mantle setup from Claude Code's own docs (`export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1`, `export AWS_REGION=…`, or the gateway trio with `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH=1` and `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL=…`) and then launches Nessy from that shell and starts a session on any Claude connection. The subprocess inherits the flag and the bundled binary routes the turn to the Bedrock Mantle endpoint instead of the endpoint the connection card in Settings shows. Because Mantle needs `anthropic.`-prefixed model IDs while our connection sends a bare/versioned Claude ID, the visible result is a failing turn — a 4xx/model-not-found surfaced as a generic session error with no hint that the request left for AWS — or, with `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH=1` and a gateway URL set, an unsigned request to the user's gateway host that appears to succeed while the configured connection was silently bypassed. The exact same shell state with `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` instead produces no such effect, because that one is stripped; the asymmetry is what a user would experience as unexplainable. Second, narrower surface: an administrator's managed `env` block that sets Mantle is applied immediately with no withhold-and-confirm prompt, while the `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` in the same block is held back and prompted — the consent dialog lists half the configuration it is protecting the user from.

#### f208 · `troubleshoot-install`

The env var name, the value we write (a full path) and the existence requirement are all correct; only the accepted-filename predicate is wrong, and it is wrong by being a strict subset. We accept `{bash.exe}`; the page specifies `{bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, sh}`. So `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe` — and the extension-less `bash`/`sh` — are refused by us and accepted by Claude and by the SDK build we bundle. Two second-order deltas ride on the same predicate: the Browse dialog's `extensions: ['exe']` filter makes the extension-less half of the enum unselectable even if the validator widened, and our reaction to a rejected name is a hard user-facing error at SET_PATH rather than the documented silent fallback-plus-`--debug`-warning (at CHECK and at startup we do fall back, but we additionally delete the persisted value, which the page does not ask for). The existence half of the validator must NOT be relaxed toward the page's "missing path also just warns": that rule is min-version 2.1.219, the bundled SDK 0.3.183 still `process.exit(1)`s on a missing path, so our existence check is protective and stays.

- **Документация связывает.** troubleshoot-install.md:664 binds the value of `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` to a file whose name is one of exactly four: `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`. "Claude Code accepts only a file named `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`; with any other name, such as Git for Windows' `git-bash.exe` launcher, it ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with `--debug`." The same line adds that a path that does not exist gets that same fallback-plus-warning, and version-gates the whole rule with `{/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}` (before 2.1.219 any existing file was used with no name check, and a missing path exited at startup).
  > Claude Code accepts only a file named `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`; with any other name, such as Git for Windows' `git-bash.exe` launcher, it ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with `--debug`.

Three live call paths depend on it, and there are two duplicated copies of the handler. (1) Onboarding SET_PATH: `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:265-274` — a failed validation returns `{ success: false, error }` and nothing is persisted or exported; the identical handler for the desktop app is `apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:189-198` (its `registerSystemCoreHandlers` is a full duplicate of server-core's, wired at :442, while the server-core one is wired for headless in `registerCoreRpcHandlers` (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/index.ts`)). (3) Startup revalidation: `apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:596-606` — an invalid persisted path is cleared, the env var deleted, and `Cleared invalid persisted Git Bash path:` logged. The refusal is surfaced verbatim in the UI: `apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useOnboarding.ts:737-751` puts `result.error` into `errorMessage`, rendered red at `apps/electron/src/renderer/components/onboarding/GitBashWarning.tsx:115-117`. - **Пользователь.** Windows only, and only when Git Bash is not at a standard `...\Git\bin\bash.exe`. A user in that position opens the onboarding Git Bash step, types or browses to the shell Git actually gave them — `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe`, or a portable/MSYS layout whose shell is `sh.exe` — presses "Use this path", and gets the red inline error "Path must point to bash.exe" (GitBashWarning.tsx:116). Onboarding will not advance past the step (useOnboarding.ts:318), so the user is stuck being told to install Git they already have, on a path the SDK we spawn would have accepted without complaint. The Browse dialog compounds it: filtered to `*.exe`, the extension-less `bash`/`sh` cannot even be selected, so the file picker shows nothing usable in that layout. If such a path ever did get persisted, the next launch silently drops it (index.ts:602-604, warning only in the main log) and onboarding re-prompts. On macOS and Linux nothing is observable — CHECK returns `{ found: true }` immediately (`.../rpc/system.ts:202-204`). Exposure is genuinely narrow because a normal Git for Windows install does ship `bin\bash.exe` and is auto-detected, which is why this has not been reported.
